jobs.title: In-House Sales Representative (Bilingual)
jobs.description_html:
If you're eager to elevate your sales career within an exciting resort environment, we've got the perfect spot for you! Exploria Resorts is seeking an accomplished In-House Sales Representative to join our award-winning team!

What does Exploria Resorts have to offer?  Serving the vacation ownership and hospitality industry for over 25 years, Exploria Resorts offers full-time employees competitive benefits including Health insurance with HSA and FSA options, Dental Insurance, Vision Insurance, Life/AD&D insurance, Short – Long- Term Disability coverage, 401(k), PTO, Paid Holidays, Employee Referral Program, Employee and Family Discounts, growth opportunities, and more!

In-House Sales Representative 

Full Time

Why join?

  • Competitive Compensation Plan: Earn 8% – 10% commission, UNCAPPED earning potential
  • Growth-Oriented Company
  • Great Culture and Leadership
  • W-2 Employment + Full Benefits Package (medical, dental, vision, PTO)
  • Employee and Family Discounts
  • Unique Brand Partnerships, including Orlando City Soccer Club
  • Exclusive Product Offering – Sell luxury vacation ownership with our high-end Exclusive Collection

Job Summary: 

The In-House Sales Executive is responsible for customer servicing, updating, and providing various sales options to Exploria LLC Vacation Club members. The primary duties of the Sales Executive are to discover the Owner’s needs & interests and create a want/need to update their membership with Exploria LLC. Conduct a 60-minute presentation with owners and present Club Exploria products in a manner to create a sale.

Responsibilities and Duties:

  • Must be able to convey information and ideas clearly, both oral and written.
  • Must work well in fast-paced, high-pressure situations.
  • Must be able to evaluate and select among alternative courses of action quickly and accurately.
  • Must be effective in handling problems in the workplace, including anticipating, preventing, identifying, and solving problems, as necessary.
  • Must be effective at listening to, understanding, and clarifying concerns and issues raised by team members and guests.
  • Follow Exploria Resorts In-House Sales processes and best practices to execute sales presentations.
  • Meet and Exceed Company In-House Sales goals.
  • All other duties assigned by management.

Qualifications

Qualifications and Skills:

  • FL Real Estate License is required
  • 2 years of In-House Timeshare Sales experience is required.
  • Bilingual in English and Spanish is preferred
  • Maintain required VPG and closing %
  • Professional, neat appearance
  • Positive attitude/Team player
  • Proper conduct at all times
  • Must be able to work weekends and holidays.

Exploria Resorts Recruitment Form

jobs.title: Security Officer
jobs.description_html:
Join us at Exploria Resorts to provide a secure, hospitable environment. Enhance guest experiences through security, collaboration, and hospitality. Your role in maintaining a secure and welcoming environment will make a difference to guests and colleagues alike. Ready to join a warm, collaborative team enhancing guest experiences through security? Apply now!

What does Exploria Resorts have to offer?  Serving the vacation ownership and hospitality industry for over 25 years, Exploria Resorts offers full-time employees competitive benefits including Health insurance with HSA and FSA options, Dental Insurance, Vision Insurance, Life/AD&D insurance, Short – Long- Term Disability coverage, 401(k), PTO, Paid Holidays, Employee Referral Program, room rate discounts, growth opportunities, and more! 

Security Officer

Full Time

$17.00/hr

Open Availability, Weekend Availability, and Holidays. 

Summer Bay Orlando by Exploria Resorts

Job Summary: 

The Security Officer is a highly visible, perpetually patrolling employee who is expected to seek out opportunities to improve the guest experience and resolve challenges in an effective and timely manner. Position is responsible for the patrol of Summer Bay Resort property for the purpose of prevention, protection, early detection, or assistance of other community services or agencies.

Responsibilities and Duties:

  • Checking equipment (ex: uniforms, vehicles, radios, emergency medical, fire fighting equipment, key, flashlights, etc,
  • Patrol of resort property for the purpose of prevention, protection, early detection, or assistance of other community services or agencies, monitoring and responding to radio communications, assisting guests as needed, recording the tour reports using the mobile device, addressing any suspicious activity immediately and responding to incidents promptly, utilize the “de-escalation” practice to help resolve disputes, and follow directions provided by Resort Management or supervisor.
  • Maintaining a working knowledge of all equipment assigned to positions
  • Proper preparation and submission of all Incident Reports according to standard operation procedures public by the company, including proper form use, timeliness, and proper documentation format
  • Receiving, storage, and properly logging evidence
  • Investigation assignments as necessary and assigned by Management
  • Checking, patrolling, and touring, and securing the properties during shift
  • Answering fire, gas, or other alarms as needed or requested on property
  • Manning the Guard House. This includes monitoring radios, answering phones, directing callers to the proper extension, providing accurate driving directions, managing the access of guests, visitors, vendors, and employees, challenging pedestrian traffic to ensure proper clearance, key control, record keeping for the shift activities, and notifying when emergency agencies arrive and depart the resort.
  • Assuring all company policies and safety regulations are reported as observed
  • Responsible for special projects or assignments for various areas as assigned by the Supervisor of the Department or Resort Management.
  • Obtaining or utilizing First Aid and related training for use within the position and for utilization, when necessary, in the field according to company guidelines
  • Attending periodic scheduled refresher training
  • Marinating a safe and clean work area for guests and employees
  • Assuring compliance of all company policies as outlined for all employees
  • Other primary duties as needed or required by business demands.

All other duties assigned my management

Qualifications

Qualifications and Skills:

  • State of Florida class D security license required.
  • Valid Driver's license required. 
  • Maintaining proficient and knowledge of Florida Criminal Code and Florida Criminal procedures
  • Must assist with minor maintenance problems as needed or available
  • Must assist with delivery of housekeeping items overnight when that department is closed.
  • May be required to handle special projects as assigned
  • Other secondary functions as necessary for the operation of the department and the company

Physical Demands:

  • Frequent walking/standing.

Exploria Resorts Recruitment Form

jobs.title: Front Desk Agent
jobs.description_html:
Don't miss this incredible opportunity to join our Exploria Resorts team and create lasting memories for our guests. If you are passionate, customer service-oriented, and dedicated, we invite you to apply today. Your journey to a fulfilling career in hospitality starts here!

What does Exploria Resorts have to offer?  Serving the vacation ownership and hospitality industry for over 25 years, Exploria Resorts offers full-time employees competitive benefits including Health insurance with HSA and FSA options, Dental Insurance, Vision Insurance, Life/AD&D insurance, Short – Long- Term Disability coverage, 401(k), PTO, Paid Holidays, Employee Referral Program, room rate discounts, growth opportunities, and more!

Front Desk Agent

Full-Time 

$16.00/Hour  

3 pm-11 pm, Weekends and Holidays are Required.  

Location: 17805 US-192 Clermont, FL 34714

Job Summary:  

The Front Desk Agent is responsible for ensuring every guest has an enjoyable experience at the resort. A few of the main duties of a front desk agent are greeting guests at the front desk, answering questions, recommending activities and restaurants to guests, and answering any phone calls.

Responsibilities and Duties:

  • Responds professionally and courteously to arriving, departing, in-house guests and potential guests
  • Checks guests in/out
  • Provides outstanding customer service to all guest
  • Respond to telephone and in-person inquiries regarding reservations, hotel information, and guest concerns

All other duties assigned by management

Qualifications

Qualifications and Skills:

  • Must have strong hospitality skills and communication skills to interact with guests in a professional manner
  • Must be able to understand and follow verbal/written instructions, work on more than one task at a time, and be able to communicate both verbally and in writing
  • Adhere to all cashiering procedures: the verification of all cash, credit card, and transactions during a given shift
  • Good computer skills and detail-oriented
  • Bi-lingual is a plus

Physical Demands:

  • Ability to stand for long periods
  • Constant computer and phone usage

Required Competencies:

  • Good communication skills with other staff and colleagues
  • Perform various projects requested by supervisors/managers
  • Ability to follow instructions
  • Detail oriented
  • Phone etiquette
  • Be able to work independently

jobs.title: Transportation Supervisor
jobs.description_html:
Day in the life:

The Transportation Supervisor provides frontline leadership and oversight of daily bus operations to ensure safe, reliable, and efficient transportation service. This position supervises and supports bus operators, monitors service performance, responds to operational issues and emergencies, and ensures compliance with LYNX policies, procedures, safety standards, and applicable regulations. 

The Transportation Supervisor plays a key role in maintaining service quality by coaching and developing bus operators, addressing performance and customer service concerns, investigating incidents and accidents, and coordinating with dispatch and other departments to resolve service disputes.  This position requires strong leadership, sound judgement, effective communication, and the ability to make timely decisions in a fast-paced, 24/7 transit environment. 

This position is considered safety-sensitive and subject to the provisions of the Substance Abuse Program Policy for Safety Sensitive Positions.

Essential Functions:

  • Perform supervisory duties in LYNX’s window dispatch, radio communications center, and field assignments. Incumbents may rotate through both assignments and are expected to obtain training and required certifications for any assignment.
  • Manages on-time dispatching of operators to ensure efficient delivery of all (but not limited to), scheduled service, stand-by assignments, “duties” (straight, split runs), part-time “duties” and “trippers” on a daily basis in adherence to the contractual provisions and using independent judgment. Ensures compliance with city, local, state, and federal laws governing transit services. Initiates communication with the city’s police, safety, and fire departments as well as local construction companies that might affect service.
  • Supervises and counsels bus operators, achieving maximum productivity and high employee morale. Monitors operators by riding the system to evaluate operator efficiency; records absenteeism and tardiness; recommends additional training when needed; writes disciplinary violations on operators; documents information used for progressive discipline in conformance with LYNX policies and the Collective Bargaining Agreement; ensures on-time performance of operators.
  • Serves on interview panels and makes recommendations for selection of potential new bus operators and/or transportation supervisors.
  • Ensures minimum variation in scheduled bus service and passenger safety through managing on-site street operations, computerized radio equipment; and independent knowledge of LYNX’s service area, applicable traffic laws, policies, procedures, and union contract.
  • Resolves day-to-day operating problems that arise, including but not limited to vehicle breakdowns, accidents, and missed or late routes. Makes appropriate decisions regarding restoring or maintaining service, using independent judgment.
  • Administers and supervises system “Picks” (new schedules and work assignments) to include, but not limited to run, holiday, and special event “Picks”.
  • Supervises the dispatching of operators in accordance with established schedules. Assigns all day standby (extra-board) assignments, “duties” (straight and split runs), part-time “duties” and “trippers” daily in accordance with LYNX policies and union contract. Responsible for approving and documenting any irregularities in scheduling such as misses.
  • Enforces departmental policies, the Work Rules, Memorandums of Agreement, procedures, and employee attendance.
  • Maintains informative communications with the public and passengers pertaining to LYNX service, schedules, and necessary changes due to emergencies and special events/circumstances. Resolves passenger disputes related to provision of service. Investigates complaints, to resolution, and communicates same.
  • Makes recommendations to management to improve operations, decrease turnaround times, and streamline work processes. Works cooperatively and jointly to provide customer service.
  • Monitors conditions of streets, bus stop areas, bus shelters, broken signposts, broken bus stop signs, overhanging tree limbs, overhanging post, etc.; reports findings as needed. Establish detours as necessary.
  • Informs Customer Service of adverse weather and road conditions, detours, schedule changes, and delays.
  • Investigates and documents employees’ injury/workers compensation claims.
  • Operates buses during emergency situations. *
  • Performs other duties or special assignments as may be required or assigned.

Required Qualifications:

  • High School diploma or G.E.D. plus two years of supervisory experience.
  • Two years of college coursework (at least 60 credit hours) in public transportation or public/business administration, or a related program; or four years of leadership experience may be substituted for required supervisory experience. Leadership experience may include line instructor, training instructor, or other relevant experience in a leadership role.
  • Must have a Florida CDL Class “B” license with airbrakes and a passenger endorsement. Or, possess a Florida CDL Class “B” permit with airbrakes and a passenger endorsement prior to hire.
  • Must possess and maintain a safe driving record.
  • Must pass a DOT physical examination and drug screen and maintain a valid medical examiner’s certificate.
  • Must be able to communicate clearly and effectively in English, both orally and in writing.
  • Must become familiar with the Collective Bargaining Agreement, Operators Guide to Daily Operations and Work Rules, and LYNX administrative rules, policies and procedures within 30 days of hire.

Desired Qualifications:

  • Previous experience in public transportation with knowledge of transit operating procedures, rules, and regulations.
  • College degree from a regionally or nationally accredited institution in public transportation or public/business administration or a closely related field.
  • Bi-lingual or multi-lingual
  • Working knowledge of CAD/AVL.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities (KSAs):

  • Working knowledge of currently used computer hardware and applicable software at an intermediate level of proficiency.
  • Ability to learn to use and effectively operate new computer hardware, software, and other communications technologies as implemented by LYNX.
  • Ability to exercise good judgment, quickly analyze situations, develop effective solutions, and adopt prescriptive courses of action.
  • Ability to train, supervise, and provide constructive feedback.
  • Ability to continually multi-task and prioritize work, meeting schedules and deadlines.
  • Ability to maintain composure in stressful situations and resolve complaints in a satisfactory manner while interacting with difficult individuals.
  • Ability to communicate effectively in English, both orally and in writing.
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, including the ability to establish and maintain positive working relationships with those encountered in the course of work using principles of excellent customer service.
  • Ability to exhibit a professional, courteous demeanor.
  • Ability to work in a diverse environment.

Work Environment and Special Considerations:

  • Works various shifts to include days, nights, Saturdays, Sundays, and holidays. This is a 24 hour/7 day a week operation.
  • Employees in this position must comply with all requirements of the Federal Transit Administration (FTA) regarding the testing of safety sensitive employees. This position is considered safety-sensitive under FTA drug and alcohol regulations (49 CFR Part 655).
  • LYNX provides the community with much needed public transportation, and it is important for the Agency to resume its services as quickly and as safely as possible in the event of any natural, technological, or human-caused emergency or disaster. This position is considered a mission critical member of LYNX’s emergency preparation and response efforts during an emergency or disaster and as such requires 24-hour availability in the event of an emergency or disaster.

Supervisors will be used to operate buses during emergency ESF-1 operations such as:

  • Shelter Operations
  • Assisted Living Transports
  • If Operators are unable to drive a bus back to the yard due to accident or incident

This will only be put in place when these situations are deemed an emergency. Transportation Supervisors will be placed in refresher training each year.

Reasonable accommodation will be made for otherwise qualified individuals with a known disability, when required by law. This description in no way states or implies that these are the only duties to be performed by the employee occupying this position. Employees will be required to follow any other job-related instructions and to perform any other job-related duties requested by their supervisor

Why Join LYNX:

We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being today and strengthen your financial security for tomorrow, including:

    • Robust Retirement Package
      • Defined contribution 401(a) plan with a 7% employer base contribution
      • 100% employer match up to 3% of employee contributions into the 457 plan
    • FREE employee‑only medical insurance 
    • Company paid life insurance and long-term disability insurance
    • Competitive medical, dental, and vision coverage
    • Short-term disability insurance available
    • Flexible Spending Accounts
    • Paid vacation, sick leave and holidays
    • Employee assistance and wellness programs
    • Access to our on‑site Employee Wellness Center
    • FREE bus transportation for you, your spouse, and dependent children

Sponsorship Notice: LYNX does not sponsor employment-based visas, including H-1B. All candidates must be legally authorized to work in the United States at the time of application and throughout the duration of employment.

STEM OPT: LYNX is not a STEM-OPT Employer.

jobs.title: Mobility Data and Compliance Specialist- Transit
jobs.description_html:
Position Description

The Mobility Data and Compliance Specialist supports LYNX Mobility Services by validating, reconciling, and analyzing data for paratransit, ADA eligibility, on-demand transportation, and contracted operations.  This position helps ensure operational, eligibility, and performance data is accurate, complete and consistent with agency standards and regulatory requirements.

Working under the direction of the Mobility Supervisor, the Specialist investigates data discrepancies, evaluates performance trends, monitors contractor reporting, and prepares reports that support operational oversight and service improvements. The role collaborates with internal teams and contracted service providers to improve data quality and reporting processes and maintain accurate, audit-ready information for dashboards, reports, and regulatory submissions. 

Shift
Monday - Friday

8:00am to 5:00pm EST

Essential Functions

This list is intended to indicate the general nature and level of work performed by employees within this classification and is not designed to be interpreted as an exhaustive listing of all tasks required of employees assigned to the job.  All employees will be expected to perform other duties as assigned. All jobs require regular and reliable attendance.

  • Collaborates with internal Mobility teams and contracted Mobility service providers to apply data quality standards, resolve discrepancies, and support accurate operational and eligibility reporting.
  • Monitors contractor data submissions and service performance metrics for compliance with Mobility Services contracts, ADA, and FTA expectations.
  • Validates data from Trapeze PASS, Trapeze Certification, scheduling/dispatch systems, and contractor platforms; prepares quality assurance and discrepancy reports for the Mobility Supervisor.
  • Develops and maintains data quality reports to track performance indicators, identify trends, and address deficiencies.
  • Supports development of dashboards, performance visualizations, and trend analyses used for operational oversight and forecasting.
  • Prepares reports and executes SQL/Crystal/Trapeze queries to support compliance monitoring, contractor oversight, ADA standards, and data integrity requirements. Supports documentation and review of contractor training records, FAC 1490 requirements, ADA-related data standards, and contractual reporting obligations.
  • Conducts spot checks of contractor trip data, contractor performance indicators, eligibility timelines, and quality assurance metrics.
  • Provides guidance to staff and contractors regarding data integrity, reporting protocols, and Mobility data workflows.
  • Provides operational support for Mobility Services data systems, including issue tracking, data validation, and coordination with Mobility operational staff.

Required Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree from a regionally or nationally accredited institution in Business Administration, Information Management, or related field.
  • Three years of experience in data analysis/quality assurance or a related field.
  • Must possess and maintain a valid Florida driver's license and safe driving record.
  • Experience working with Mobility Services data systems (paratransit, ADA eligibility, on‑demand, or Trapeze PASS/CERT).

Desired Qualifications:

  • Five years of data analysis experience in mobility services.
  • Experience supporting contractor compliance reporting or ADA/FTA performance metrics.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities (KSA)

  • Proficiency in using Microsoft Office applications, including Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Access, and Outlook.
  • Knowledge of database structures, data Queries, and reporting principles.
  • Knowledge of ADA, FTA, and NTD reporting requirements.
  • Knowledge of Trapeze PASS, Trapeze Certification, dispatch/scheduling systems, and contractor data platforms.
  • Strong analytical skills with the ability to collect, organize, interpret, and present data with accuracy and attention to detail.
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a collaborative team.
  • Ability to problem-solve and determine root causes of data anomalies.
  • Ability to prepare clear and concise reports, dashboards, and visualizations.
  • Ability to work in a diverse environment.
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, including the ability to establish and maintain positive working relationships with those encountered in the course of work using principles of excellent customer service.
  • Ability to exhibit a professional, courteous demeanor.
  • Ability to work in a diverse environment.

Work Environment and Special Considerations

  • Works in an office environment and requires long periods seated.
  • This position requires close visual acuity to perform an activity such as viewing a computer terminal and extensive reading.
  • This position requires the ability to verbally express or exchange ideas by means of spoken word and the ability to hear sounds at normal speaking levels, to receive information through oral communication and to make fine discriminations in sound.
  • Any employee using a company vehicle must possess a valid Florida driver’s license and maintain a safe driving record. 

Support Personnel Workforce Member: LYNX provides the community with much needed public transportation, and it is important for the Agency to resume its services as quickly and as safely as possible in the event of any natural, technological, or human-caused emergency or disaster. This position is considered support personnel of LYNX’s emergency preparation and response efforts during an emergency or disaster and as such, shall be expected to return to their normal work schedule as soon as possible or when otherwise notified after the emergency has occurred.

Reasonable accommodation will be made for otherwise qualified individuals with a known disability, when required by law. This description in no way states or implies that these are the only duties to be performed by the employee occupying this position.  Employees will be required to follow any other job-related instructions and to perform any other job-related duties requested by their supervisor. 

Why Work at LYNX?

We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being today and strengthen your financial security for tomorrow, including:

  • Robust Retirement Package
  • Defined contribution 401(a) plan with a 7% employer base contribution
  • 100% employer match up to 3% of employee contributions into the 457 plan
  • FREE employee‑only medical insurance 
  • Company paid life insurance and long-term disability insurance
  • Competitive medical, dental, and vision coverage
  • Short-term disability insurance available
  • Flexible Spending Accounts
  • Paid vacation, sick leave and holidays
  • Employee assistance and wellness programs
  • Access to our on‑site Employee Wellness Center
  • FREE bus transportation for you, your spouse, and dependent children

jobs.title: Customer Service Representative - Transit (Hybrid)
jobs.description_html:
Job Summary

Help Central Florida stay connected as a Customer Service Representative also known at LYNX as the Mobility Service Representative.  In this role, you will assist riders with trip planning, bus routes and schedules, fares, and service updates, primarily through incoming calls and other customer communication channels.  

You will answer questions, address concerns with patience and professionalism, document customer interactions, and coordinate with operations staff to provide accurate, timely information.  This position requires strong communication skills, attention to detail, and the ability to navigate computer systems while assisting customers.

Schedule & Work Assignment

Sunday-Thursday, 9:00am to 6:00pm, with Friday's and Saturday's off. This hybrid position includes four remote workdays and one onsite workday per week. Employees must work remotely within Central Florida and have reliable transportation and flexibility to report onsite or cover customer service assignments as operation needs require. 

Essential Functions:

This list is intended to indicate the general nature and level of work performed by employees within this classification and is not designed to be interpreted as an exhaustive listing of all tasks required of employees assigned to the job.  All employees will be expected to perform other duties as assigned. All jobs require regular and reliable attendance.

  • Works as part of the customer service team in the Mobility Services department delivering excellent customer service.
  • Responds to customer concerns in a professional and empathetic manner, escalating issues when necessary to ensure resolution.
  • Keeps hold/wait times to a minimum and adheres to call center/customer service performance metrics.
  • Communicates regularly with operations staff regarding scheduling, cancellations, and passenger issues.
  • Records and tracks customer calls, inquiries, and concerns using appropriate software systems; updates and maintains monthly reports.
  • Stays informed of all policy changes, service updates, detours, and bulletins to provide accurate information.
  • Assists with mail-outs for rider guides, schedules, and other informational materials.
  • Supports team members by covering assignments during absences and assisting with training as needed.

Customer Service Call Center Position Focus & Work Environment: 

  •  
  • Answers incoming calls promptly for fixed-route services, providing accurate schedule, routing, and   system-wide information using Schedule books, maps, trip planning tools, and schedule brochures.
  • Records accurate and detailed trip information while providing emergency call support during unexpected service interruptions.
  • Provides Estimated Time of Arrival (ETA) updates to passengers and communicates any delays or changes. 
  • Maintains up-to-date passenger records in customer database; makes all necessary changes to key fields during call. 
  • Ability to work remotely within the Central Florida area; must have reliable transportation and flexibility to cover office-based areas based on operational needs. 
  •  

Ticket Sales Window Position Focus & Work Environment:  

  • Operates the ticket sales window at LYNX Central Station, delivering patient, high-quality customer service and accurately and efficiently processing cash and electronic transactions.
  • Handles overflow calls to help stabilize service levels and ensure consistent customer experience during high-volume periods.
  • Works in a confined area and requires long periods seated.

Lost and Found Position Focus & Work Environment: 

  • Operates the lost and found window at LYNX Central Station, assisting customers with inquiries and ensuring proper documentation and follow-up
  • Works in a confined area and requires long periods seated. Occasionally works in a warehouse environment, which may include exposure to weather conditions.
  • Uses a company vehicle to collect lost and found items from LYNX properties, which requires the ability to lift up to 50 pounds and the ability to possess and maintain a valid Florida Driver’s license and safe driving record.

Required Qualifications:

  • High School Diploma or GED, plus three years of clerical, data entry, and computer software experience and at least one year of customer service experience provided in person or by telephone.
  • Additional directly related experience beyond the minimum requirement may substitute for the required education on a year-for-year basis.

Desired Qualifications:

  • Three years of experience performing face-to-face customer service duties and/or call center experience.
  • Government, public sector, and/or transit work experience.
  • Bilingual or multilingual. 

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities (KSAs):

  • Customer Service Excellence: Demonstrated ability to provide outstanding service, maintain professionalism, and resolve customer concerns with empathy and efficiency.
  • Transit System Knowledge: Understanding of fixed-route and paratransit operations, scheduling processes, and trip planning tools.
  • Technical Proficiency: Ability to operate computer systems and learn department-specific software, including scheduling platforms, mapping tools (e.g., Google Maps), and call tracking systems.
  • Communication Skills: Strong verbal and written communication skills to convey accurate information and instructions clearly to diverse audiences.
  • Interpersonal Skills: Ability to build positive relationships with customers, colleagues, and operations staff while working collaboratively in a team environment.
  • Attention to Detail: Skill in accurately recording trip details, maintaining passenger records, and ensuring data integrity across multiple systems.
  • Time Management & Multitasking: Ability to prioritize tasks, manage multiple queues, and meet performance metrics in a fast-paced environment.
  • Cash Handling: Competence in processing ticket sales and managing financial transactions securely and accurately.
  • Problem-Solving & Adaptability: Ability to identify solutions for customer issues, adapt to policy changes, and respond effectively during service disruptions or emergencies.

Special Consideration

  • This position requires close visual acuity to perform an activity such as viewing a computer terminal and extensive reading.
  • This position requires the ability to verbally express or exchange ideas by means of spoken word in English.
  • Any employee using a company vehicle must possess a valid Florida driver’s license and maintain a safe driving record. 

HIPAA Workforce Member: As a HIPAA Workforce Member, the incumbent in this position will be requested to sign a Confidentiality Agreement affirming their obligation to maintain confidentiality of all employees’ Personal Health Information (PHI). Newly hired HIPAA Workforce Members will be trained within four weeks of hire. In the event a newly hired HIPAA Workforce Member fails to complete this training within the applicable timeframe, they may be reassigned to a position that does not have access to PHI, or appropriate corrective action up to and including termination may be taken. Upon separation of employment or access to PHI, whichever is earlier, each HIPAA Workforce Member will be requested to sign an Acknowledgement of Continued Obligation to Maintain Confidentiality of PHI. 

Mission Critical Workforce Member: LYNX provides the community with much needed public transportation, and it is important for the Agency to resume its services as quickly and as safely as possible in the event of any natural, technological, or human-caused emergency or disaster. This position is considered a mission critical member of LYNX’s emergency preparation and response efforts during an emergency or disaster and as such, will be asked to work during these emergencies or disasters. Therefore, mission critical team members are required to prepare their homes and family for the impending emergency at least 48 hours in advance.

Reasonable accommodation will be made for otherwise qualified individuals with a known disability, when required by law. This description in no way states or implies that these are the only duties to be performed by the employee occupying this position.  Employees will be required to follow any other job-related instructions and to perform any other job-related duties requested by their supervisor. 

 

Why Work at LYNX?

We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being today and strengthen your financial security for tomorrow, including:

  • Robust Retirement Package
    • Defined contribution 401(a) plan with a 7% employer base contribution
    • 100% employer match up to 3% of employee contributions into the 457 plan
  • FREE employee‑only medical insurance 
  • Company paid life insurance and long-term disability insurance
  • Competitive medical, dental, and vision coverage
  • Short-term disability insurance available
  • Flexible Spending Accounts
  • Paid vacation, sick leave and holidays
  • Employee assistance and wellness programs
  • Access to our on‑site Employee Wellness Center
  • FREE bus transportation for you, your spouse, and dependent children

jobs.title: Diesel & CNG Electronic Systems Technician
jobs.description_html:
Job Description

LYNX is seeking an experienced Diesel & CNG Electronic Systems Technician also known at LYNX as a Technician A - Electronics to inspect, diagnose, maintain, and repair electronic and electrical systems used in transit operations. Equipment includes fair boxes, destination signs, communication systems, video recording equipment, and other onboard electronic devices.  This position performs preventative and corrective maintenance, troubleshoots complex system failures, interprets wiring diagrams and schematics, and tests equipment to verify reliable operation.  The technician also documents repairs and provides technician guidance to other technicians while following established safety procedures. 

This position is considered safety-sensitive and subject to the provisions of the Substance Abuse Program Policy for Safety Sensitive Positions.

Shifts: Must be willing and able to work any and all shifts below as LYNX is a 24/7 operation and this will include weekends and holidays:

  • 6:00am to 2:30pm 
  • 4:00am to 2:30pm 
  • 6:00pm to 4:30am (This shift comes with a $2.00 pay differential)

Essential Functions

  • Completes scheduled and non-scheduled maintenance on all electronic systems, subassemblies and control devices.
  • Inspects, diagnoses, removes, and repairs electronic systems, equipment and devices.
  • Records periodic electrical testing and recommends modification or replacement of equipment that fails to meet acceptable operational standards.
  • Diagnoses the cause of electrical or mechanical malfunction or failure of operational equipment and performs preventive or corrective maintenance.
  • Applies electrical theory and related knowledge to test and repair operational electrical and electrical controlled equipment and circuitry.
  • Adjusts, calibrates, aligns and modifies circuitry and components, and records effects on unit performance.
  • Analyzes and interprets test data.
  • Develops charts, graphs and schematics to describe and illustrate system’s operating characteristics, malfunctions, deviations from design specifications and functional limitations for consideration by management in broader determinations affecting system design.
  • Uses testing equipment (meters, oscilloscopes, test bench and mock-up).
  • Executes field repairs on all electronic systems, subassemblies and control devices including connector and harness manufacture and repair.
  • Works with lower-grade technicians on difficult or unusual problems.
  • Ensures operator defects are completed on all electrical equipment on schedule.
  • Sets up standard test apparatus or devices, test equipment and circuitry to conduct functional, operational, environmental, and live test to evaluate performance and reliability of production models.
  • Performs other duties as may be required or assigned.

Required Qualifications

  • High School diploma or GED plus four years’ experience in the electronic repair field plus two years of technical school; or an equivalent combination of education, training and experience.
  • Electronic Technician Degree helpful.
  • Must possess and maintain a current Florida CDL permit/license, Class “B” with Passenger endorsement and Airbrakes.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

  • Knowledge of electronics to inspect, diagnose, remove and repair equipment and systems.
  • Knowledge of occupational hazards and safety precautions of the trade.
  • Ability to work with minimal supervision.
  • Ability to read electrical wiring diagrams and schematics
  • Ability to work in a fast-paced environment.
  • Ability to work as a team player.
  • Ability to drive buses, trucks, non-revenue vehicles and equipment into the shop, line and yard.
  • Ability to physically bend, stoop, walk, kneel, stretch and lift fifty pounds.
  • Ability to work days, nights, weekends, and holidays.
  • Ability to pass DOT physical and drug screen.
  • Ability to understand and operate special test equipment.
  • Ability to work in open bays, inside buses and inside test and repair room.
  • Ability to work with commercial cleaners and toxic materials.
  • Ability to effectively communicate in English, both orally and in writing.
  • Ability to provide own advanced tools.
  • Ability to learn new skills and take initiative.
  • Ability to exhibit a professional, courteous demeanor.
  • Ability to work in a diverse environment.
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, including the ability to establish and maintain positive working relationships with those encountered in the course of work using principles of excellent service.

Work Environment and Special Considerations 

Employees in this position must comply with all requirements of the Federal Transit Administration (FTA) regarding the testing of safety sensitive employees.  This position is considered safety-sensitive under FTA drug and alcohol regulations (49 CFR Part 655).

LYNX provides the community with much needed public transportation, and it is important for the Agency to resume its services as quickly and as safely as possible in the event of any natural, technological, or human-caused emergency or disaster. This position is considered a mission critical member of LYNX’s emergency preparation and response efforts during an emergency or disaster and as such, requires 24-hour availability in the event of an emergency or disaster.

Reasonable accommodations will be made for otherwise qualified individuals with a known disability, when required by law. Job Summary:

Help keep Central Florida moving by maintaining the buses that serve our community. LYNX is seeking a Fleet Maintenance Technician B - Diesel & CNG, also known as a Technician B to perform preventative maintenance, diagnose mechanical problems, and repair transit buses and related equipment. Responsibilities include servicing engines, transmissions, brakes, steering, suspension, basic electrical systems, and air conditioning components. 

This position works alongside higher-level technicians on complex repairs and assists with road calls and vehicle recovery when needed.  The successful candidate brings experience in transit or heavy vehicle maintenance, strong troubleshooting skills, and a commitment to safe, reliable fleet operations. This is a safety-sensitive position. 

This position is considered safety-sensitive and subject to the provisions of the Substance Abuse Program Policy for Safety Sensitive Positions.

Shifts: Must be willing and able to work any shift below including weekends and holidays:

  • 6:00am to 2:30pm
  • 2:00pm to 10:30pm
  • 10:00pm to 6:30am
  •  

Essential Functions:

  • Completes scheduled and non-scheduled maintenance on all systems and safety equipment on transit coaches for safe operations.
  • Carries out ordinary mechanical, hydraulic or structural maintenance repairs and adjustments.
  • Determines the source of trouble.
  • Repairs or replaces defective parts or makes changes as instructed.
  • Refers difficult or unusual problems to higher grade employees for guidance or repair.
  • Executes field repairs on road failures and tows buses if necessary.
  • Tunes and repairs on road failures and tows buses if necessary.
  • Repairs engines: replaces all major engine components including cylinder heads
  • Replaces transmission; replaces all external components.
  • Replaces engine/transmission assemblies and accessories.
  • Diagnoses and repairs air systems and components and relines brakes.
  • Repairs and replaces all steering and suspension components.
  • Performs basic electrical diagnoses and repairs on electrical systems; replaces components.
  • Performs major repairs, component replacement and Schedule “A” and “C” inspections on wheelchair lifts.
  • Performs minor repairs and replaces A/C components.
  • Performs other duties as may be required or assigned.

Required Qualifications:

  • High School diploma or GED plus three years’ experience in transit or heavy vehicle maintenance and one year of technical school; or an equivalent combination of education, training and experience.
  • Must possess and maintain a current Florida CDL permit/license, Class “B” with Passenger endorsement and Airbrakes.

  • Knowledge of occupational hazards and safety precautions of the trade.
  • Ability to work with limited supervision.
  • Ability to bend, stoop, walk, stretch, kneel, and lift 50 lbs.
  • Ability to work as part of a team.
  • Ability to work days, nights, weekends and holidays.
  • Ability to pass a DOT physical and drug screen.
  • Ability to work in open bays, inside buses and outside in varying weather conditions.
  • Ability to handle and use commercial cleaners and toxic materials to perform duties.
  • Ability to provide own tools.
  • Ability to effectively communicate in English, both orally and in writing.  
  • Ability to exhibit a professional, courteous demeanor.
  • Ability to work in a diverse environment.
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, including the ability to establish and maintain positive working relationships with those encountered in the course of work using principles of excellent service.

jobs.title: Maintenance Training Instructor (Diesel & CNG)
jobs.description_html:
Join Our Team and Drive Excellence in Fleet Maintenance!

Are you a skilled diesel or heavy vehicle maintenance professional with a passion for teaching and developing others? LYNX is seeking a Maintenance Training Instructor (Diesel & CNG) to lead, develop, and deliver engaging technical training programs that empower our maintenance team to keep Central Forida moving safely and efficiently. 

In this impactful role, you'll combine your hands-on maintenance expertise with your ability to train, mentor, and inspire technicians at all levels.  From developing training materials and conducting hands-on instructions to evaluating program effectiveness and supporting regulatory compliance, you'll play a key role in building a highly skilled workforce that supports one of the region's largest public transportation systems. 

This position is considered safety-sensitive and subject to the provisions of the Substance Abuse Program Policy for Safety Sensitive Positions.

Hours of Operation:

Monday-Friday 6am-2:30pm but can work any 8-hour shifts that are needed and we are open 7 days a week depending on training needs, some shifts might be overnight. We are a 24/7 operation; however, we will provide advanced notice 

Day in the Life:

This position develops, coordinates, implements, conducts and evaluates training programs for maintenance personnel in the proper service, repair and maintenance of buses, support vehicles, and shop equipment.
This position is considered safety‐sensitive and subject to the provisions of the Substance Abuse Program Policy for Safety Sensitive Positions.
Essential Functions: This list is intended to indicate the general nature and level of work performed by employees within this classification and is not designed to be interpreted as an exhaustive listing of all tasks required of employees assigned to the job. All employees will be expected to perform other duties as assigned. All jobs require regular and reliable attendance.

In conjunction with the above, the Diesel Maintenance Instructor will:


• Consults with Maintenance department leadership for input in developing maintenance training programs.
• Delivers effective training programs by applying strong presentation, training and facilitation skills, and delivering feedback to learners; develops action plans and measures the impact to the organization.
• Prepares, plans, organizes and conducts maintenance training needs assessments and analyses, lesson plans, course curricula, visual and mechanical aides, written materials and hands‐on instruction that complies with internal procedures and external mandates or regulations.
• Participates as a resource to maintenance management on safety, technical proficiency and productivity issues, and works with the safety division to develop and implement programs compliant with state and national regulations, to promote the safety and well‐being of Authority employees.
• Coordinates, evaluates and monitors internal and external vendor training programs.
• Monitors and evaluates the effectiveness of training programs by measuring changes in skill levels and improvements demonstrated by maintenance personnel and modifies programs accordingly to improve effectiveness to the quality vehicle maintenance training programs.
• Ensures that all training materials are updated as needed, for new equipment, new procedures, technical information, etc.

Required Qualifications:

• Associate’s degree from a regionally or nationally accredited institution in automotive or diesel technology or related field, plus four years of experience working in heavy vehicle maintenance to include two years of experience conducting training programs; or combination of related experience, education and training.
• Additional directly related experience beyond the minimum requirement may substitute for the required education on a year-for-year basis.
• Must possess and maintain a Florida Class “B” CDL with airbrakes and passenger endorsement, or be able to obtain one within 6 months, have an acceptable driving record, and the ability to pass a DOT physical examination and drug screen.

Desired Qualifications:

• Experience as a presenter/facilitator of leadership and technical training, or previous training experience in a transportation or technical field.
• Bilingual (English/Spanish) helpful.


Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities (KSAs):

• Knowledge of training theory, methods of presentation, theories of learning,     appropriate modes of presentation and other related training issues for adult‐     learners.
• In‐depth knowledge of all heavy vehicle and facilities systems pertinent to the    Authority’s vehicles to include, but not limited to, mechanical systems, fuel   systems, hydraulic systems, pneumatic systems, HVAC, brake systems,   multiplexed systems, electrical/electronic systems, etc.
• Knowledge of tool usage, problem diagnostics and test processes.
• Knowledge of industrial safety rules, regulations, including, but not limited to   US Federal Motor Carrier Safety Regulations, CFR Title 49 and Florida   Administrative Code 14‐90, hazardous materials handling and storage   regulations as applied to bus maintenance.
• Knowledge of the principles of preventive maintenance and keeps abreast of   new technologies and methodologies in the vehicle maintenance field.
• Ability to develop clear, concise and effective curricula, schedules, course   materials, audio/visual aids, administrative and technical procedures.
• Ability to work from and understand verbal instruction, blueprints, schematics,   diagrams, vendor manuals and manufacturer’s specifications.

jobs.title: Senior HR Generalist - Employee & Labor Relations
jobs.description_html:
LYNX, Central Florida’s Regional Transportation Authority, is seeking an experienced Senior Human Resources Generalist to join our HR team. This role is ideal for a seasoned HR professional who thrives in employee and labor relations and excels in conducting workplace investigations.

About the Role (This is an on-site position)


This Senior HR Generalist role will serve as a key resource for employees and leadership, with a primary focus on employee/labor relations and workplace investigations.  This position supervises one HR Generalist and reports directly to the Manager of Human Resources. This role supports a unionized, public-sector environment and ensures our processes uphold collective bargaining agreements, agency policies, and due process standards.

In addition to investigations, the ideal candidate brings broad HR knowledge and can seamlessly support other functional areas such as benefits, recruitment, policy administration, onboarding, and performance management.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead and conduct neutral, timely investigations into workplace performance issues, general misconduct, safety violations, and policy infractions.
  • Prepare clear, comprehensive, and legally defensible investigative reports; assist managers in drafting their reports to ensure accuracy and compliance.
  • Ensure all investigatory processes comply with collective bargaining agreements, agency policies, and due process requirements, including representation rights.
  • Provide guidance to leadership on disciplinary actions, grievance processes, and labor relations matters.
  • Identify trends and recommend proactive solutions or training to address systemic issues.
  • Support HR operations including recruitment, benefits administration, onboarding, HRIS updates, policy interpretation, and employee support.
  • Collaborate across teams to uphold LYNX’s values of respect, collaboration, care, and leadership.

Ideal Candidate Profile

  • Minimum of 5 years of HR Generalist experience, including at least 2 years focused specifically on employee/labor relations and investigations.
  • Demonstrated experience conducting investigations and writing investigative reports in a unionized and/or public-sector environment.
  • Strong knowledge of collective bargaining agreements, investigatory due process standards, and documentation requirements.
  • Skilled communicator with the ability to present findings, coach managers, and build positive working relationships.
  • Ability to work with independence, sound judgment, and high attention to detail.
  • Broad HR experience across multiple functional areas such as benefits, recruitment, and policy administration.
  • Experience with HRIS systems (Dayforce, Oracle HCM preferred).
  • Bachelor’s degree in HR, Business/Public Administration, or a related field.

Why Work at LYNX?

We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being today and strengthen your financial security for tomorrow, including:

  • Robust Retirement Package
    • Defined contribution 401(a) plan with a 7% employer base contribution
    • 100% employer match up to 3% of employee contributions into the 457 plan
  • FREE employee‑only medical insurance 
  • Company paid life insurance and long-term disability insurance
  • Competitive medical, dental, and vision coverage
  • Short-term disability insurance available
  • Flexible Spending Accounts
  • Paid vacation, sick leave and holidays
  • Employee assistance and wellness programs
  • Access to our on‑site Employee Wellness Center
  • FREE bus transportation for you, your spouse, and dependent children

Sponsorship Notice: LYNX does not sponsor employment-based visas, including H-1B. All candidates must be legally authorized to work in the United States at the time of application and throughout the duration of employment.

STEM OPT: LYNX is not a STEM-OPT Employer. 

 ******************************************************************************************************************************************************

JOB DESCRIPTION:

The Senior Human Resources Generalist is responsible for providing daily support for our Human Resources programs and policies including employee relations, investigations, training, HRIS maintenance, onboarding, policy implementation, change management and employment law compliance. The position serves as a key resource for employees and leadership.

Essential Functions:

This list is intended to indicate the general nature and level of work performed by employees within this classification and is not designed to be interpreted as an exhaustive listing of all tasks required of employees assigned to the job. All employees will be expected to perform other duties as assigned. All jobs require regular and reliable attendance. 

Supervision and Team Leadership 

Plans, coordinates, supervises, and evaluates the work of assigned staff; administers work assignments and monitors deadlines, meets with staff regularly to identify and resolve problems; counsels’ employees to correct deficiencies and takes corrective action as necessary.

Employee Relations and Investigations 

Investigations: Conducts neutral and timely investigations into allegations of general misconduct, including but not limited to:

  • Violations of workplace rules, policies, and procedures
  • Insubordination, dishonesty, misuse of government resources
  • Performance-related misconduct and safety violations
  • Unprofessional conduct and ethics violation

Compliance: Ensures investigatory processes comply with CBAs, agency policies, and due process standards. Ensures employee representation rights are honored during investigatory interviews (e.g. Weingarten rights). Supports disciplinary processes by providing investigative findings, documentation, and testimony for grievances.

Training: Develops and delivers training on investigatory procedure, interview best practices, documentation standards, and non-EEO policy compliance for managers and HR partners

Reporting Writing: Prepares clear, comprehensive investigative reports outlining findings of fact, credibility assessments, and policy or rule analysis. Ensures reports are legally defensible and suitable for use in disciplinary actions, grievance hearings, or arbitration.

  • HRIS Entry: Tracks investigations to ensure contractual timelines and procedural requirements are met.
  • Analysis: Identifies trends or systemic issues related to employee conduct and recommends corrective actions or training.
  • HR Generalist Support: Provides support in benefits, onboarding, policy interpretation, and performance management. Serve as a resource for employees and supervisors on HR procedures and best practices.
  • Budget Planning and Financial Oversight: Assists with the development of accurate budget forecasts. Manages assigned budgets in alignment with organizational goals and fiscal policies. Analyzes financial data to ensure responsible allocation of resources and proactively identify opportunities for efficiency and cost savings.

Benefits and Retirement 

  • Benefits Administration: Oversee the administration of employee benefits programs including medical, dental, vision, life insurance, disability, and voluntary benefits. Serve as the primary point of contact for employee benefits inquiries and vendor coordination.
  • Retirement Plans: Oversees the administration of retirement programs such as defined benefit pensions, 401(a), 457(b), or other public sector retirement plans. Coordinate with plan providers, ensure compliance with plan rules and IRS regulations, and assist employees with enrollment, changes, and retirement planning resources.
  • Open Enrollment & Communication: Leads the annual open enrollment process, including planning, system updates, employee communications, and coordination with benefits carriers. Develop and deliver clear, accessible materials and presentations to educate employees on benefit offerings.
  • Compliance & Reporting: Ensures compliance with all applicable laws and regulations, including ACA, HIPPA, COBRA, FMLA, and retirement plan requirements. Prepare and submit required reports and filings, such as 1095-C’s, and retirement plan audits. 

Leave Management:

  • Administers leave programs including FMLA, short- and long-term disability, and other statutory or company-sponsored leave policies. Coordinate with payroll and department managers to ensure accurate tracking and communication.
  • HR Generalist Support: Provides support in employee relations, onboarding, policy interpretation, and performance management. Serve as a resource for employees and supervisors on HR procedures and best practices.
  • Process Improvement: Evaluates and recommend improvements to benefits and retirement processes, systems, and employee experience. Stay current on industry trends and legislative changes affecting benefits and retirement programs.
  • HRIS Entry: Coordinates activities involving status changes; enters all information into HRIS in accordance with policies/procedures; ensures promotions/demotions are in compliance with policies/procedures; verifies salary changes and ensures inclusion of correct information.
  • Budget Planning and Financial Oversight: Assists with the development of accurate budget forecasts. Manages assigned budgets in alignment with organizational goals and fiscal policies. Analyzes financial data to ensure responsible allocation of resources and proactively identify opportunities for efficiency and cost savings.

Required Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree from a regionally or nationally accredited institution in Human Resources Management, Business or Public Administration or a closely related field plus five years of experience as an HR generalist to include a minimum of two years of experience in each assigned area of specialization; or a combination of related education, training and experience sufficient to successfully perform the essential duties at the level indicated.
  • Additional directly related experience beyond the minimum requirement may substitute for the required education on a year-for-year basis.
  • Experience with HRIS software such as Dayforce and/or Oracle HCM.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Government, public sector, and/or transit work experience.
  • Experience working in a union environment
  • SPHR/PHR or SHRM-SCP/SHRM-CP, CBP or other HR-related certification

Knowledge, Skills, & Abilities (KSA's):

  • Knowledge of the principles and practices of benefits, compensation, employment, and employee/labor relations.
  • Knowledge of collective bargaining agreements and unions.
  • Ability to exercise independent judgement and initiative within established guidelines.
  • Ability to analyze and identify employee, administrative, operational, and organizational issues; evaluate alternatives and reach sound, logical, and fact-based conclusions; develop sound and persuasive recommendations.
  • Ability to collect, evaluate, and interpret data in statistical and narrative forms; ability to use qualitative and quantitative analysis, tools, and reviews.
  • Ability to demonstrate personal initiative, follow-through, and accountability.
  • Ability to lead, train, evaluate, and supervise staff, project team members, and/or external vendor staff.
  • Proficiency using computer and related technology, including proficiency with Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook), the internet, and knowledge of HRIS applications.
  • Ability to exhibit a professional, courteous demeanor.
  • Ability to work in a diverse environment.
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, including the ability to establish and maintain positive working relationships with those encountered in the course of work using principles of excellent customer service.

Work Environment & Special Considerations:

  • Works in an office environment and requires long periods seated.
  • This position requires close visual acuity to perform an activity such as viewing a computer terminal and extensive reading.

jobs.description_html:
*We are currently accepting applications for Bus Operator positions**

 


 LOCAL Driving Only for Fixed Route
 Full Time Hours GUARANTEED
 FREE Employee Only Health Insurance 
  Life Insurance
 Paid Holidays
 Paid Vacation & Sick Leave
 Employee Wellness Center
 Retirement Contribution (401A) with Match
 Dental, Vision, Short-Term & Long-Term Disability Insurance Available
 Yearly Pay Increases Based on Union Contract Up to Current Top Pay - $34.25 /hourly 

Information you need to know before applying:

  • You must possess a valid Florida CDL license; Class A or B with AIRBRAKES and PASSENGER endorsement to apply.
  • Must be able to work days, nights, Saturdays, Sundays, holidays, split shifts, split days off, and any hours assigned.
  • Must be 21 years of age.
  • Must be able to successfully pass the LYNX Bus Operator Training Program.
    • Training is 8 weeks long.
    • Attendance and punctuality are mandatory.
    • No absences allowed during training.
    • Hours during training vary and will include some weekends. Training start times may be as early as 4:00am.   

If you receive a conditional job offer, you will need to:

 

  • Provide copies of credentials such as diplomas and licenses
  • Complete and pass a DOT pre-employment drug test and DOT physical examination and receive a Medical Examiner’s Certificate with at least a one-year expiration date.
  • Successfully pass a thorough pre-employment background check to include criminal background and employment verifications.
  • Have an acceptable driving record.

Sponsorship Notice: LYNX does not sponsor employment-based visas, including H-1B. All candidates must be legally authorized to work in the United States at the time of application and throughout the duration of employment. 

NOTE: Applications are reviewed as received and only those applicants who fully meet the established qualifications will be contacted by HR to participate in the screening process.


____________________________________________________________________________

JOB SUMMARY:

  • Bus Operators transport passengers by operating any type of passenger bus on regularly scheduled links (fixed routes), observing all state and municipal traffic laws, observing all safety rules strictly adhering to time schedules, and providing exceptional customer service.

SAFETY SENSITIVE:

 

  • This position is considered safety-sensitive and is subject to drug and alcohol testing, including but not limited to pre-employment testing, post-accident testing and random testing, under Federal Transportation Administration (FTA) drug and alcohol regulations, and U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) regulations, 49 CFR Part 40 and Part 655.

EXAMPLES OF RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Safely operates passenger buses.
  • Performs DOT pre-trip inspections.
  • Answers passenger questions courteously.
  • Provides exceptional customer service.
  • Learns and adheres to assigned driving routes.
  • Observes all state and municipal traffic laws.

jobs.title: Sr.maintenance Technician A- Diesel & CNG
jobs.description_html:
Join the team that keeps Central Florida moving!

LYNX is seeking a skilled and motivated Senior Maintenance Technician A - Diesel & CNG, also known as Technician "A", to perform diagnostics, repairs, inspections, and preventative maintenance on our fleet of transit vehicles and support equipment. This position offers the opportunity to work with advanced vehicle systems including diesel engines, electrical systems, HVA, brakes, steering, suspension, and hybrid technologies in a safety focused environment.

The ideal candidate is mechanically inclined, enjoys problem-solving, and takes pride in delivering quality repairs that ensure safe and reliable transportation for our community.

As a member of a bargaining unit, this position follows a seniority-based system for bidding on shifts and days off.

Hourly Pay Rate: $32.62 - $38.38 depending on qualifications

Shifts: Must be willing and able to work any and all shifts below as LYNX is a 24/7 operation and this will include weekends and holidays:

  • 6am to 2:30pm
  • 2pm to 10:30pm ($2.00 additional dollars and hour for pay differential)
  • 10:00pm to 6:30am ($3.00 additional dollars and hour for pay differential)
  •  

Technician "A" Essential Job Functions:

  • Carries out ordinary mechanical, hydraulic or structural maintenance repairs and adjustments.
  • Determines the source of trouble; repairs or replaces defective parts or makes changes as instructed.
  • Works from written or verbal instructions, blueprints, schematics, diagrams, vendor manuals and manufacturer’s specifications to accomplish work.
  • Applies diagnostic and analytical tools in problem solving.
  • Is competent in the use of testing equipment such as compression testers, engine/transmission readers, multimeters, AMP meters, logic probes and exhaust gas analyzers.
  • Executes fields repairs on road failures and tows buses if necessary.
  • Provides assistance to lower grade mechanics when instructed.
  • Diagnoses, tunes and repairs engines; replaces all major components including cylinder heads and other major engine components.
  • Diagnoses, repairs and replaces all electronic engine and transmission controls and sensors and wiring harness.
  • Diagnoses and repairs transmissions; replaces all internal sensors/solenoids and all major components.
  • Diagnoses, repairs and replaces battery electric and hybrid bus components such as; controls, drive motors, inverters and battery packs.
  • Replaces engine/transmission assemblies and accessories.
  • Diagnoses and repairs air systems and components and relines brakes.
  • Diagnoses, repairs and replaces all steering and suspension components.
  • Diagnoses and repairs all wiring harnesses.  Replaces components in electrical subsystems.
  • Diagnoses, repairs and replaces all components of wheelchair lifts.  Executes A and C inspections.
  • Diagnoses, repairs and replaces all A/C components.
  • Performs other duties as may be required or assigned.

Required Qualifications:

  • High School diploma or GED plus four years’ experience in transit or heavy vehicle maintenance plus two years of technical school; or an equivalent combination of education, training and experience.
  • Must possess and maintain a current Florida CDL permit/license, Class “B” with Passenger endorsement and Airbrakes.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:

  • Knowledge of occupational hazards and safety precautions of the trade.
  • Ability to work with minimal supervision.
  • Ability to bend, stoop, walk, stretch, kneel, and lift 50 lbs.
  • Ability to work as part of a team.
  • Ability to work nights, weekends and holidays.
  • Ability to pass DOT physical and drug screen.
  • Ability to work in open bays, inside buses and outside in varying weather conditions.
  • Ability to work with commercial cleaners and toxic materials.
  • Ability to effectively communicate in English, both orally and in writing.
  • Ability to read electrical schematics.
  • Ability to provide own tools.
  • Employees must be able to communicate in English on the work site.
  • Ability to exhibit a professional, courteous demeanor.
  • Ability to work in a diverse environment.
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, including the ability to establish and maintain positive working relationships with those encountered in the course of work using principles of excellent service.

 

Work Environment and Special Considerations:

  • Employees in this position must comply with all requirements of the Federal Transit Administration (FTA) regarding the testing of safety sensitive employees.  This position is considered safety-sensitive under FTA drug and alcohol regulations (49 CFR Part 655).

Why Work at LYNX?

We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being today and strengthen your financial security for tomorrow, including:

  • Robust Retirement Package
    • Defined contribution 401(a) plan with a 7% employer base contribution
    • 100% employer match up to 3% of employee contributions into the 457 plan
  • FREE employee‑only medical insurance 
  • Company paid life insurance and long-term disability insurance
  • Competitive medical, dental, and vision coverage
  • Short-term disability insurance available
  • Flexible Spending Accounts
  • Paid vacation, sick leave and holidays
  • Employee assistance and wellness programs
  • Access to our on‑site Employee Wellness Center
  • FREE bus transportation for you, your spouse, and dependent children
