jobs.title: Cloud Security Engineer III (AI/ML Platforms)
jobs.description_html:
Are you looking to make an impactful difference in your work, yourself, and your community? Why settle for just a job when you can land a career? At ICW Group, we are hiring team members who are ready to use their skills, curiosity, and drive to be part of our journey as we strive to transform the insurance carrier space. We're proud to be in business for over 50 years, and its change agents like yourself that will help us continue to deliver our mission to create the best insurance experience possible.


Headquartered in San Diego with regional offices located throughout the United States, ICW Group has been named for the twelfth consecutive year in a row and for the 20th time overall as a Top 50 performing P&C organization offering the stability of a large, profitable and growing company combined with a focus on all things people. It's our team members who make us an employer of choice and the vibrant company we are today. We strive to make both our internal and external communities better everyday! Learn more about why you want to be here!


PURPOSE OF THE JOB

The purpose of the Cloud Security Engineer III is to design secure architectures and develop cybersecurity approaches and techniques for the security of any cloud or SaaS solution. This position will assist with strategic initiatives for short and long-term plans to identify and reduce the attack surface across cloud, SaaS and on premises applications and systems, which may include support for AI/ML platforms such as data pipelines, model development environments, and model serving infrastructure.

This position is responsible for keeping the cloud and/or AI/ML platform infrastructure current, making recommendations, and participating in the implementation and continuous improvement of technologies and services in cloud-based and machine learning environments.

The position exists to monitor and defend ICW Group’s technology—which may include cloud platforms, SaaS solutions, and AI/ML systems—against potential threats that jeopardize the financial growth, data integrity, and security goals of the Company.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Monitors and defends cloud-based information systems against unauthorized access, modifications and/or destruction.

  • Monitors networks and systems for security breaches, using software that detects intrusions and anomalous system behavior and develops strategies to respond to and recover from a security breach. 

  • Leads security incident response, including preparation, detection, analysis, containment, eradication, and recovery.

  • Researches and implements methods to remediate network and application security vulnerabilities.

  • Leads and participates in security controls reporting, compliance audits, monthly and ad-hoc statistics and trends, and risk-focused reports including internal and 3rd party Risk Assessments.

  • Utilizes automated tools to identify, assess, and report security concerns, with emphasis placed on effective communication to stakeholders. Takes an active lead to inform, advise, and partner with business units to help better secure operations.

  • Provides management of cloud security solutions/platforms including access management and data protection, coordination of security services, and support during incident cases.

  • Directs and influences multi-disciplinary teams in implementing and operating Cyber Security controls.

  • Collaborates with internal teams to support implementation of security best practices.

  • Collaborates with application developers and database administrators to deliver creative solutions to difficult cloud technology challenges and business requirements.

Leads and runs complex cloud security related projects and resolves security related issues.

  • Resolves complex security projects and issues. Develops a set of security standards to respond to and recover from a security breach focused on cloud , SaaS and/or AI/ML systems.

  • Provides support by proposing solutions, coordinating implementation, and enforcing information systems security policies, standards, and methodologies.

  • Uses advanced technologies including Intrusion Detection & Prevention Systems, Lambda, CloudFront, CloudFormation, AWS Security Hub, S3, Batch, API Gateway, VPC, IAM, KMS, CloudWatch, CloudTrail, SFTP, DynamoDB and Config, etc.

  • Prepares and analyzes system security reports by collecting, analyzing, and summarizing data and trends, systems usage and access patterns, and makes recommendations to improve security.

  • Maintains cloud operational security posture to ensure information system security policies, standards, and procedures are established and followed.

  • Creates and updates technical cloud security standards for assets and software.

  • Provides subject matter expertise on cloud information security architecture and systems engineering to other IT and business teams.

  • Executes security architectures for cloud cloud/hybrid systems.

Serves as cloud cyber security technical subject matter expert, trainer and a primary resource for the organization.

  • Provides cloud information security expertise to system development teams throughout the development life cycle process.

  • Partners with internal teams to ensure system design and implementation are consistent with company policies, requirements, and directives.

  • Leads and conducts information security risk assessments including documenting processes, service level agreements and best practices.

  • Develops the overall cloud security design, development, testing, and implementation of security solutions. Recommends compliance strategies that support customer requirements and alignment to company policy.

  • Ensures cloud security quality, adherence to security guidelines/controls, profitability, and information security related metrics for self and assigned projects.

  • Collaborates with key stakeholders on remediation strategies and follows remediation activities through closure.

  • Provides support on Incident Response on security incidents and participates in the development of business cases and presentations on information security technologies of interest to the company.

  • Counsels project teams, application owners, and other Information Security teams on cloud information or AI/ML security controls.

Partners with project management and other internal teams in determining overall security solutions.

  • Executes technical and process changes required to adopt, maintain, and adjust security controls as required to manage the company's risks and align with industry best practices.

  • Works with peers in other internal groups to drive technical security risk down in targeted areas.

  • Takes end-to-end ownership of one or more security tools and metrics, driving risk down actively across the company.

  • May support administration and monitoring of tools used for AI/ML environments.

  • Contributes to the continual enhancement, understanding and adoption of the IT security practices through governance, core processes, leading technology, and enhancement of team’s skill sets.

  • Coaches and educates others to increase early detection rates and decrease IT risk and security.

AI/ML RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Assists in monitoring AI/ML platforms for anomalous behavior such as unusual model access patterns, unexpected data usage, or irregular inference activity.

  • Assists in identifying and remediating vulnerabilities in AI/ML pipelines, including insecure configurations and access control gaps.

  • Collaborates with data scientists and ML engineers to help implement secure AI/ML solutions aligned with business requirements.

  • Gains familiarity with ML platform tooling (e.g., model registries, pipeline orchestration tools) and applies security best practices to their use.

  • Develops foundational knowledge of AI/ML security concepts and contributes to team knowledge sharing.

  • Supports implementation of security controls for AI/ML systems and related infrastructure.

  • Develops awareness of emerging AI/ML security risks and communicates relevant observations to the team.

  • Shares knowledge and learns from senior engineers regarding AI/ML security practices.

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

This position has no supervisory responsibility but may mentor and train junior engineers.

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

  • Bachelor's Degree required in Engineering, Cybersecurity, Networking, Computer Science, Data Science, or related field.

  • Minimum 8 years of experience working in a security engineering related role designing secure networks, systems and application architectures or equivalent combination of education and experience required.

  • Minimum 3-5 years of experience in AWS Cloud Security services required.

  • Experience in cyber security role requiring knowledge of data analysis, risk assessment, risk mitigation, investigation methods, incident management concepts and practices, and policy and procedure development.

  • Exposure to or experience with AI/ML platforms, data pipelines, or analytics environments preferred.

  • Basic understanding of ML lifecycle concepts and data handling practices preferred.

CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS

  • Certification in GSEC, CISSP, and/or Security+ preferred.

  • AWS Certified Security – required.

  • AWS Developer or Solutions Architect Associate - Security Emphasis preferred.

  • AI/ML or data-related certifications are a plus but not required.

KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS

  • Direct experience using advanced technologies such as Intrusion Detection & Prevention Systems (IDS/IPS), Firewalls, SIEM, Antivirus software, Network Packet Analyzers, content filtering, Malware analysis and forensics tools to detect intrusions.

  • Experience with AWS Services such as AWS Identity & Access Management, AWS Organizations, AWS Security HuB, Guard Duty, CloudTrail, AWS CloudTrail.

  • Knowledge of risk assessment tools, technologies, and methodologies.

  • Knowledge of disaster recovery, computer forensic tools, technologies, and methods. Knowledge of enterprise security platforms. 

  • Ability to communicate network security issues to peers and management.

  • Strong understanding of endpoint security solutions to include File Integrity Monitoring and Data Loss Prevention.

  • Demonstrated experience as a lead engineer in the design, implementation and support in an enterprise IT environment.

  • Ability to hypothesize on root cause of inefficiencies and then test out probable solutions against those hypotheses.

  • Must be able to read, write and speak English effectively.

  • Ability to effectively communicate/present technical information to a non-technical audience.

  • Ability to cross train and share information with team members.

  • Basic understanding of AI/ML security concepts such as data protection, access control, and model usage risks.

  • Familiarity with ML-related components such as data pipelines and model deployment environments is a plus.

  • Willingness to learn model risk and AI governance concepts.

  • Understanding of data privacy considerations in analytics and ML environments is a plus.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS 

Office environment – no specific or unusual physical or environmental demands and employees are regularly required to sit, walk, stand, talk, and hear.  Employees are required to reach with hands and arms; stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl.  Employees must occasionally lift and/or move up to 30 pounds.  Employees are required to have visual acuity and be capable of operating and viewing computers and other electronic devices for extended periods of time.

WORK ENVIRONMENT 

This position operates in an office environment and requires the frequent use of a computer, telephone, copier, and other standard office equipment.

We are currently not offering employment sponsorship for this opportunity.

#LI-HYBRID


The current range for this position is

$121,624.81 - $217,710.99

This range is exclusive of fringe benefits and potential bonuses. If hired at ICW Group, your final base salary compensation will be determined by factors unique to each candidate, including experience, education and the location of the role and considers employees performing substantially similar work.


WHY JOIN ICW GROUP?

  • Challenging work and the ability to make a difference
  • You will have a voice and feel a sense of belonging
  • We offer a competitive benefits package, with generous medical, dental, and vision plans as well as 401K retirement plans and company match
  • Bonus potential for all positions

PURPOSE OF THE JOB


The Senior Claims Examiner position handles moderate to complex claims with a focus on providing the highest level of service for policyholders and ICW Group to independently bring claims to an equitable conclusion within Company standards and best practice guidelines. The Senior Claims Examiner works with a sense of urgency, understands insurance coverage concepts, and navigates the legal system with the support of counsel to drive strategic outcomes.


ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES


Manages all aspects of  a moderate to highly complex  claims inventory.

  • Effectively communicates with policyholders, agents, attorneys, and witnesses to gather information and provide the highest possible level of customer service.
  • Promptly investigates claims to determine exposure, works with appropriate experts and makes strategic recommendations.
  • Utilizes appropriate resolution tactics (e.g., mediation, negotiation, denial, litigation or offer) to proactively drive outstanding results.
  • Operates within the requirements of related state and/or the governing entity rules and regulations as well as internal claims handling policies and procedures. 
  • Directs defense counsel throughout the litigation process in line with ICW litigation guidelines while monitoring legal fees and costs.

All Claims Examiners:

  • Consistently provides exceptional customer service.
  • Effectively collaborates with team members from various departments for project and process discussions.

  • Acts as a mentor and provides training for less experienced team members.

Workers’ Compensation Claims (Specific Responsibilities):

  • Prepares and presents claims status reports for internal and external stakeholders.
  • Administers timely and appropriate benefits to injured workers; manages and approves payment of benefits within designated authority level.  Works within applicable state rules, regulations as well as ICW Group’s internal claims handling policies and procedures.
  • Creates and adjusts reserves in a timely manner to ensure reserving activities are consistent with company policies.
  • Resolves claims fairly and equitably, acting in the best interest of the insured while providing timely benefits to injured workers as required by law.
  • Provides technical guidance and collaborates with leadership on complex claim resolution strategies and specialty handling initiative
  • Handles specialized claim inventories involving complex medical exposure, litigation, fatality, PTD, life pension, or long-term resolution strategies.
  • Identifies and drives resolution opportunities on complex or long-duration claims through proactive settlement, reserving, and medical management strategies.

This position has no supervisory responsibility

Bachelor's degree (or equivalent combination of education and experience) required along with a minimum of 5+ years’  related claims handling experience required; complex litigated claims experience is highly preferred.

  • Excellent verbal communication skills, time management, attention to detail and organizational skills
  • Must be adept at learning new technology

PURPOSE OF THE JOB 

The purpose of this job is to assist the Workers Compensation legal department by providing technical support to attorneys, conducting legal research and drafting legal documents. This role will work under the supervision of assigned attorneys to assist in court and trial related research.  


ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Performs analysis and research functions for Workers’ Compensation cases.

  • Drafts legal memos and briefs.
  • Prepares motions and petitions as well as opposition/response to same.
  • Analyzes and researches legal and factual issues.
  • Secures documentation from employers and third parties to support litigation analysis.
  • Develops templates involving legal motions and petitions.
  • Assists in deposition and trial preparation and supports legal team throughout the entire litigation process.
  • Researches and analyzes law sources to prepare draft memoranda, briefs or arguments for review, approval and use by attorneys.
  • Communicate with clients, court staff, and law firms by telephone and written correspondence.
  • May attend depositions, mediations, court hearings, and trials.
  • Tracks and records time through litigation management system. 

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

This role does not have supervisory responsibilities. 


EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

Bachelors degree required.  Currently attending an accredited law school with 2 semesters/3 quarters completed with passing grades.  Legal or insurance experience preferred.


CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS 

None required. 


KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS

Interest in learning CA workers compensation litigation. Proficient use of a personal computer and skills with Microsoft Word, Excel, Outlook, Adobe, PowerPoint, EAMS, and litigation management systems.  Knowledge and use of general office equipment such as scanners and copiers. Familiarity with business legal principles. Demonstrated experience working independently under minimal supervision, maintaining a strong work ethic, and exercising initiative.  Ability to communicate effectively both verbally and in writing.  Ability to read and understand legal materials.  Ability to keep information organized and confidential. Ability to effectively present information, verbally and in writing, including English usage, spelling, vocabulary, grammar, and punctuation.  Strong organizational abilities, time management, and aptitude for learning new skills. Ability to prioritize multiple tasks and complete timely. Strong analytical and critical thinking skills. 


PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS

Office environment – no specific or unusual physical or environmental demands and employees are regularly required to sit, walk, stand, talk, and hear.

This position operates in an office and court environment and requires frequent use of a computer, telephone, copier, scanner, and other standard office equipment.

PURPOSE OF THE JOB

The purpose of this job is to serve as the first point of contact to process new injuries reported by customers. This position exists to ensure that initial requests from customers are handled thoughtfully and thoroughly, while following Company standards and procedures.


ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Provides excellent customer service as the first point of contact for customers.

  • Provides customer care and service to insureds.
  • Answers all incoming inquiry calls directed by general switchboard.
  • Receives and intakes new initial claim documentation either via phone, e-mail, or fax and enters into claim systems.
  • Responds to insureds in a timely manner.
  • Directs questions to the appropriate contact in the department. 

Inputs new claims into enterprise resource planning (ERP) system as well as creates written documentation including physical file for manual storage.    

  • Reviews insurance policy information to determine coverage.
  • Completes data entry for all first reports of injury.
  • Determines severity of injuries and advises the appropriate levels of staff within standard operating procedures. 

Communicates with insureds, agents, internal and external stakeholders, as necessary. 

  • Assists examiners in contacting insureds or other involved persons to obtain missing or incomplete information to process claim.
  • Receives and/or returns telephone calls as directed by claim examiner.
  • Responds to insureds, agents or outside participants, as directed.
  • Processes incoming mail and other administrative duties relating to claims.

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

This role does not have supervisory responsibilities.


EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

High school diploma or general education degree (GED) required.  Minimum 1 year of related experience and/or training; or, equivalent combination of education and experience.


CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS

None required.


KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS

Working knowledge or familiarity with customer service techniques, principles and practices.  Insurance industry understanding, a plus. Ability to read, write and comprehend simple instructions, short correspondence, and memos. Ability to effectively present information in one-on-one and small group situations to customers, clients, and other employees of the organization. Ability to add, subtract, multiply, and divide using whole numbers, common fractions, and decimals.  Ability to compute rate, ratio, and percent and to draw and interpret bar graphs.

jobs.description_html:
Are you looking to make an impactful difference in your work, yourself, and your community? Why settle for just a job when you can land a career? At ICW Group, we are hiring team members who are ready to use their skills, curiosity, and drive to be part of our journey as we strive to transform the insurance carrier space. We're proud to be in business for over 50 years, and its change agents like yourself that will help us continue to deliver our mission to create the best insurance experience possible.


Headquartered in San Diego with regional offices located throughout the United States, ICW Group has been named for the twelfth consecutive year in a row and for the 20th time overall as a Top 50 performing P&C organization offering the stability of a large, profitable and growing company combined with a focus on all things people. It's our team members who make us an employer of choice and the vibrant company we are today. We strive to make both our internal and external communities better everyday! Learn more about why you want to be here!


PURPOSE OF THE JOB 

The Manager, Organizational Change Management leads the people-side adoption capability within the Strategy & Transformation Office. This role establishes and operates a repeatable OCM methodology that helps the organization prepare for, adopt, and sustain changes to business processes, systems, roles, ways of working, and operating models. The role ensures major initiatives are supported by change impact assessments, stakeholder engagement, communication and training plans, readiness measures, and adoption metrics, so transformation outcomes are realized and sustained after delivery. 


ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES 


Builds and Leads the Enterprise OCM Capability 

  • Defines and maintains the enterprise change management methodology, standards, templates, and artifacts used across major initiatives. 
  • Establishes consistent expectations for change impact assessment, stakeholder analysis, sponsor alignment, readiness planning, communication, training, adoption measurement, and reinforcement. 
  • Builds OCM capability across project teams, business leaders, people managers, and change practitioners through coaching, tools, and repeatable practices. 

Leads Change Strategy and Adoption Planning 

  • Partners with portfolio, architecture, delivery, business, HR, and communications leaders to identify the operational and people impacts of each major initiative. 
  • Develops change strategies and plans that support adoption of new processes, systems, roles, policies, organizational structures, and ways of working. 
  • Ensures initiatives entering governance and delivery have clear change risks, stakeholder impacts, readiness needs, communication plans, training plans, and adoption success measures. 

Drives Stakeholder Engagement, Communication, Training, and Readiness 

  • Creates stakeholder maps, engagement plans, sponsor roadmaps, communication plans, training strategies, and readiness assessments for enterprise initiatives. 
  • Coaches executives, sponsors, people managers, and project leaders on their roles in leading change and supporting impacted teams through transition. 
  • Coordinates with HR, Internal Communications, Training, business leaders, and delivery teams to align messaging, learning, timing, and reinforcement activities. 

Measures Adoption and Reinforces Sustained Change 

  • Defines adoption, readiness, utilization, proficiency, sentiment, and reinforcement metrics for major initiatives. 
  • Monitors change progress and identifies adoption risks, resistance patterns, training gaps, and reinforcement needs. 
  • Reports change readiness and adoption health into STO governance forums so adoption outcomes are reviewed alongside delivery, portfolio, and architecture metrics. 

Leads OCM Team Operations and Continuous Improvement 

  • Plans and manages OCM capacity, work intake, prioritization, and resource assignment across the transformation portfolio. 
  • Maintains OCM artifacts, playbooks, lessons learned, and reusable assets to improve consistency and speed across initiatives. 
  • Identifies opportunities to improve change governance, stakeholder engagement, communications, training, and adoption measurement practices. 

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES 

May directly supervise change management practitioners, analysts, communications/training resources, or adoption specialists as the function matures. Carries out supervisory responsibilities in accordance with company policies and applicable laws, including interviewing, hiring, training, planning and assigning work, coaching and developing staff, setting performance expectations, conducting performance reviews, addressing issues, and managing team capacity and priorities. 


EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE 

  • Bachelor's degree from a four-year college or university required, preferably in Business Administration, Organizational Development, Communications, Human Resources, Psychology, Information Systems, or a related field; Master's degree preferred. 
  • Minimum 8 years of progressive experience in organizational change management, business transformation, organizational development, communications, training, or related transformation roles. 
  • Experience leading change management for enterprise technology, process, operating model, or business transformation initiatives. 
  • Experience coaching executives, sponsors, people managers, and project teams through complex organizational change. 

CERTIFICATES AND LICENSES 

Prosci Change Management Certification or equivalent OCM credential required. ACMP Certified Change Management Professional (CCMP), PMP, SAFe, Agile, or related transformation certification preferred. 


KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS 

  • Strong knowledge of structured change management methodologies, tools, and practices, including stakeholder analysis, impact assessment, readiness planning, communication, training, adoption, and reinforcement. 
  • Ability to translate complex transformation objectives into practical change strategies that help employees understand, adopt, and sustain new ways of working. 
  • Excellent executive communication, facilitation, coaching, stakeholder engagement, and influence skills. 
  • Strong analytical skills and ability to define and use adoption, readiness, utilization, proficiency, and sentiment metrics to guide interventions. 
  • Comfort working across business, technology, HR, communications, training, portfolio, and delivery teams in a matrixed environment. 
  • Ability to manage change fatigue, resistance, competing priorities, and stakeholder concerns with sound judgment and practical mitigation plans. 

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS 

This job operates in a professional office environment. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to talk or hear. The employee frequently will sit, stand, walk, and bend during working hours. Requires manual and finger dexterity and eye-hand coordination. May be required to lift light objects. Requires normal or corrected vision and hearing corrected to a normal range. 


WORK ENVIRONMENT 

This position operates in an office environment and requires the frequent use of computer, telephone, copier, and other standard office equipment. 


This description is a general statement of essential job functions and responsibilities. 

The position may include other duties as assigned.

CDMP (Certified Data Management Professional-Practitioner or Master), Certified Data Governance & Stewardship Professional (DGSP) from ICCP (Institute for Certification of Computing Professionals), or other Data Governance Certification (DGQP) preferred.

jobs.description_html:
Are you looking to make an impactful difference in your work, yourself, and your community? Why settle for just a job when you can land a career? At ICW Group, we are hiring team members who are ready to use their skills, curiosity, and drive to be part of our journey as we strive to transform the insurance carrier space. We're proud to be in business for over 50 years, and its change agents like yourself that will help us continue to deliver our mission to create the best insurance experience possible.


Headquartered in San Diego with regional offices located throughout the United States, ICW Group has been named for the twelfth consecutive year in a row and for the 20th time overall as a Top 50 performing P&C organization offering the stability of a large, profitable and growing company combined with a focus on all things people. It's our team members who make us an employer of choice and the vibrant company we are today. We strive to make both our internal and external communities better everyday! Learn more about why you want to be here!


PURPOSE OF THE JOB

The purpose of the Senior Managing Litigation Attorney is to oversee a team of attorneys ranging from entry level to seasoned senior litigation management attorneys.  This position is responsible for overseeing and reviewing work performed by attorneys to ensure compliance with defense counsel guidelines.  The role works to improve processes, as well as assists with budget planning, financial measures and results. The Senior Managing Attorney will identify and lead initiatives to improve the team’s efficiency and ensures effective communication between the legal and business teams.  This role acts as both a Litigation Attorney with a reduced case count and manages a staff of Litigation attorneys. The position works autonomously and under the general supervision of the Litigation Management’s department Director.

This is a hybrid position, offering the flexibility to work from both home and the office. Candidates must be able to work from one of our California branch offices in San Diego, Pasadena, or Rancho Cordova.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Directs the operations of law office personnel providing litigation and legal services.

  • Oversees the law office activities to ensure efficient operations of In-House Counsel.

  • Determines the intake and assignment of cases to ensure distribution based on each attorney’s level of expertise and associated location (region or county).  

  • Achieves the departments and company goals by making strategic business decisions.

  • Ensures the firm is achieving its client satisfaction goals by evaluating productivity and quality of service. 

  • Identifies, makes recommendations for work process improvements and follows through to implement remediations. 

  • Works with leadership to ensure the department meets financial and ROI goals, identifies trends, prepares reports, and implements modifications as needed.

  • Mentors less experienced attorneys and ensures the team continues to expand their job-related knowledge, skills and abilities.

  • Regularly reviews cases and provides feedback on legal strategies, compliance with deadlines, timeliness on response, and maximizing the department’s core goals.

Provides litigation services and is responsible for all aspects of assigned Workers’ Compensation matters.

  • Handles a reduced caseload of litigated files and ensures files are fully worked and moved to resolution.

  • Litigates workers’ compensation cases in California before all state and federal courts, administrative boards, and other court proceedings.

  • Represents ICW Group, its related entities and insureds before administrative boards, state and federal courts, Court of Appeal, and the California Supreme Court.

  • Analyzes complex legal and factual issues; conducts extensive, well-reasoned legal research, as necessary; independently develops and presents defense strategies on behalf of ICW Group.

  • Provides strategic legal advice, recommendation, and implementation of clear, cost-effective, and efficient plans of action.

  • Assists in analyzing, reviewing, and distributing information on new legislation, regulations, and court decisions.

Provides oversight of a team of Litigation Management professionals.

  • Oversees the entire employee lifecycle from identifying, training, coaching and retaining talent.

  • Supervises and evaluates, mentors, motivates, and develops attorneys to strengthen the legal team.

  • Communicates clear performance expectations for the assigned team as well as providing support and guidance for achieving the department’s metric, billable hours and expectations.

  • Communicates and enforces team values including mission statement of In-House Counsel (IHC) and ICW.

  • Establishes and maintains the overall work cadence and, in partnership with Department leadership, ensures performance and outcomes strive for excellence in delivery and customer experience.

  • Acts as a resource for team members to answer questions and assist in the solution to complex problems.

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

Directly supervises employees within the Litigation Management team and carries out supervisory responsibilities in accordance with company policies and applicable laws. These responsibilities include interviewing, hiring, and training employees; planning, assigning, and directing work; conducting performance and salary reviews; rewarding and disciplining employees; addressing complaints and resolving problems; coaching, mentoring, and developing team members to further their skills and knowledge; creating and monitoring development plans; setting performance expectations/goals; forecasting staffing needs and planning for peak times and absences; enforcing department policies and procedures.

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

  • Bachelor’s degree from four-year college or university required.  Juris Doctorate from an accredited law school required. 

  • Minimum 10 years’ workers’ compensation legal experience handling complex cases along with a minimum of 2 years’ experience managing associate through senior litigation attorneys.  

CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS

Licensed and in good standing with the State Bar of California with no history of public or private reprisals.

KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS

  • Good computer skills with MS Office (including MS Excel with the ability to create financial/performance reports). 

  • Proficient in the use of applications/programs to create automated reports, templates, systems and data retrieval of high quality and reliability.

PURPOSE OF THE JOB

The Triage Examiner serves as the initial point of contact and manages claims during the early phase of the claim lifecycle (typically the first 10 days) in alignment with Company standards, best practices, and applicable laws and regulations. With a strong sense of urgency, the Triage Examiner drives early intervention to positively influence claim outcomes, optimize efficiency, and ensure a smooth transition to the next specialized claim examiner for ongoing management, while establishing a professional and positive tone that supports effective claim handling.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONIBILITIES

  • Manages the early phase of the claims lifecycle by administering benefits to injured workers in accordance with statutory case law as well as pertinent regulations for the first 10 days of the claim.

  • Contacts and interviews injured workers, witnesses, medical providers, attorneys, agents, and policyholders to obtain information necessary for claim investigation and decision-making.

  • Communicates claim activity and processing with the injured worker and policyholder.

  • Makes initial compensability recommendations and evaluates benefit eligibility within assigned authority in accordance with applicable state laws and regulations, as well as ICW Group’s internal claims handling policies and procedures.

  • Creates  reserves in a timely manner consistent with company standards and best practices guidelines.

  • Establishes accurate claim setup, including coding, documentation, and file notes, in alignment with Company standards.

  • Identifies risks, complexities, or escalation needs and refers matters to leadership as appropriate.

  • Develops initial action plans and sets claim diaries to support effective claim handling and transition.

  • Ensures a seamless and timely transition of claims to the next specialized claim examiner, including clear documentation, defined next steps, and appropriate claim direction.

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

This role does not have supervisory responsibilities.

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

  • High school diploma or general education degree (GED) required.  Bachelor’s degree from four-year college or university preferred.

  • Minimum 2-3 years’ insurance claims such as auto, property, liability, workers’ compensation or related experience required. 

  • At least 1+ year(s) of experience as a Triage Claims Associate or in a closely related workers’ compensation claim’s role.

  • Bilingual in Spanish preferred.

CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS

  • California Only: All examiners must receive certification (Self Insurance (SIP) or Workers’ Compensation Claims Examiner designation) that meets the minimum standards of training, experience, skill, and further education as required. 

  • All other jurisdictions: State Workers’ Compensation License as required.

  • Must obtain certifications within 1 year of hire into this role.

KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS

  • Basic understanding of laws and jurisdictional restraints to manage injuries.

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills, time management and organizational skills. 

  • Requires a high level of attention to detail. 

  • Team oriented and a sense of urgency for execution.

  • Able to resolve conflicts fairly and equitably.

  • Problem solving and decision-making ability.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS 

Office environment – no specific or unusual physical or environmental demands and employees are regularly required to sit, walk, stand, talk, and hear. 

WORK ENVIRONMENT 

This position operates in an office environment and requires the frequent use of a computer, telephone, copier, and other standard office equipment.

jobs.description_html:
Are you looking to make an impactful difference in your work, yourself, and your community? Why settle for just a job when you can land a career? At ICW Group, we are hiring team members who are ready to use their skills, curiosity, and drive to be part of our journey as we strive to transform the insurance carrier space. We're proud to be in business for over 50 years, and its change agents like yourself that will help us continue to deliver our mission to create the best insurance experience possible.


Headquartered in San Diego with regional offices located throughout the United States, ICW Group has been named for the twelfth consecutive year in a row and for the 20th time overall as a Top 50 performing P&C organization offering the stability of a large, profitable and growing company combined with a focus on all things people. It's our team members who make us an employer of choice and the vibrant company we are today. We strive to make both our internal and external communities better everyday! Learn more about why you want to be here!


ABOUT ICW GROUP 

ICW Group is a national, multi-line insurance carrier with an AM Best rating of 'A', approximately 1,300 employees, and headquarters in San Diego, California. ICW Group is executing an enterprise AI strategy that treats AI as core infrastructure: built on a single enterprise platform, governed by a single framework, and deployed under regulatory oversight from day one. As AI moves into underwriting, claims, and operational decisions, disciplined governance is what allows ICW to adopt AI quickly and defensibly. 

ABOUT THE AI GOVERNANCE OFFICE 

The AI Governance Management Office is ICW's standing execution and coordination function for artificial intelligence, sponsored by the SVP and Chief Digital and AI Officer. It serves the AI Governance Executive Committee (AIGEC) as its operational arm, turning AIGEC's policy, risk, and approval decisions into coordinated, well-governed delivery. The Office is the single operational home for AI intake, prioritization, coordination, enablement, and transparency.  

The Office is also ICW's single coordination point for NAIC AI Systems Evaluation Tool response preparation. California, ICW's domiciliary state, is participating in the 2026 NAIC pilot, which creates an active compliance window for the organization's higher-risk AI systems in underwriting and claims. 

PURPOSE OF THE JOB   

The AI Governance Manager is an advanced professional individual contributor within the AI Governance Management Office, reporting to the Director of Cloud, AI, ML, and Enablement Platforms. This dedicated position works independently with limited oversight to administer, facilitate, and execute AI governance day to day: coordinating the governance committees, operating the intake-to-decision workflow, owning the AI Hub, and maintaining the governance artifacts and evidence that keep ICW audit-ready and regulator-ready.  

Working closely with leadership and management at all levels, control functions, business owners, and external stakeholders, the AI Governance Manager makes governance practical and efficient so that teams move through it rather than around it. AIGEC and its subcommittees set policy, risk tolerance, and approvals; this role translates those decisions into consistent, well-documented execution, leads governance projects and processes, and provides guidance, coaching, and review of work products contributed by lower-level professionals and cross-functional partners. 

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES 

Governance Operations and Lifecycle Management 

  • Coordinate and administer AIGEC and its AI Risk & Compliance and Third-Party AI Governance subcommittees: run the cadence (intake triage, risk review, forums), prepare review packs, and document decisions and action items to closure. 

  • Operate the intake-to-decision workflow -- apply the risk taxonomy (Tier 0 through Tier 4), move each use case through the lifecycle gates with required signoffs and triggered control-function reviews, resolve intake or escalation issues, and maintain the decision log, exception register, and escalation paths. 
     

Policy, Standards, Controls, and Inventory 

  • Maintain the AI policy, standard, procedure, and control library with clear owners and review cadence, coordinate rollout of the policy suite (including the prohibited-use list), keep governance templates current, support control sufficiency testing for Tier 1 and Tier 2 systems, and recommend process and control enhancements that improve governance performance across the function. 

  • Administer the AI Systems Registry as the single audit-ready inventory of AI use cases, models, agents, and vendor AI, enforce the registry gate before build or deploy, guide business and technical owners through registry requirements, and coordinate model and system cards with lineage and classification for higher-risk systems. 

AI Hub Ownership 

  • Own and operate the AI Hub on SharePoint as the enterprise's single front door for AI serving approximately 1,300 employees -- intake, approved tools, responsible-use guidance, governance materials, learning, and metrics -- managing the content lifecycle and running it as the interface between AIGEC and the workforce. 

NAIC Regulatory Compliance Coordination 

  • Serve as the NAIC Response Coordinator, or lead significant portions of the response, for California DOI AI Systems Evaluation Tool inquiries, coordinate cross-functional evidence collection, maintain the artifacts serving Exhibits A through D (AI Systems Registry, model cards, AI Data Element Registry with Data Services, and the risk classification methodology), and track readiness and related policy updates as the pilot evolves. 

Monitoring, Audit Readiness, and Reporting 

  • Operate the governance KPI and KRI dashboard and produce reporting for AIGEC and executive leadership, assemble audit-ready evidence packs for Tier 1 systems, run regulatory scanning (NIST AI RMF, NAIC, ISO/IEC 42001, state AI laws), and route material changes into policy and control updates with operational recommendations. 

Training, Awareness, and Change Management 

  • Coordinate role-based AI governance training, attestation, and change-triggered learning, support the governance champion network and cultural-change activities, and provide guidance, coaching, and review of governance work products to reinforce clear ownership and consistent governance behavior. 
     

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES 

This role does not have direct supervisory responsibilities. 

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE 

  • Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Information Technology, Risk Management, or related field, or equivalent experience.  

  • Minimum of ten years of experience in program or project management, governance, risk, or compliance operations within a technology, IT, or regulated environment. 

  • Demonstrated experience independently operating a governance, risk, or compliance program, including committee coordination, decision logging, evidence management, escalation management, and cross-functional process improvement. 

  • Experience with AI/ML programs, digital transformation, or technology transformation initiatives, or a strong record of ramping quickly on new governance domains. 

  • Advanced facilitation, stakeholder-management, and influencing skills, with the ability to navigate technical and business audiences at all levels of the organization, and influence practices, procedures, and policies at an operational level 

  • Proficiency with collaboration and tracking tools such as Jira, Confluence, Smartsheet, or equivalent, and experience with SharePoint content management. 

  • Excellent written and verbal communication, including the ability to produce executive-level packs, dashboards, regulatory response materials, and reporting. 

  • Extensive working understanding of governance frameworks and compliance requirements in regulated industries, including the impact of governance decisions on business, technology, risk, and control functions 

  • Experience in the insurance or financial services industry preferred. 

  • Familiarity with AI governance frameworks: NIST AI RMF, ISO/IEC 42001, the NAIC AI Model Bulletin, and the NAIC AI Systems Evaluation Tool (Exhibits A through D) preferred. 

  • Experience with NAIC regulatory requirements or Department of Insurance examination processes preferred. 

  • Familiarity with the AI and ML platforms in use at ICW (AWS Bedrock, Snowflake Cortex) and enterprise AI tools (Claude Enterprise, Microsoft 365 Copilot) preferred. 

  • Experience with SharePoint site design and enterprise portal management. 

CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS  

  • Risk, audit, or governance certification such as CRISC or CGEIT, or a project and program management certification such as PMP or PgMP, or SAFe / Lean Portfolio Management preferred. 

KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS 

  • Governance Discipline: Advanced ability to operate and improve governance processes, cadence, controls, and evidence, so decisions are defensible, repeatable, and scalable across the enterprise. 

  • Facilitation: Ability to run committees, reviews, and cross-functional decisions across diverse technical and business teams, and to influence operational practices, procedures, and policies within and outside the immediate job function. 

  • Detail Orientation: Meticulous attention to governance artifacts, compliance documentation, and registry data integrity. 

  • Communication: Ability to synthesize technical, business, and regulatory information into clear, actionable materials for business owners, control functions, vendors, and executive leadership. 

  • Ownership and Project Leadership: Self-directed execution across multiple concurrent governance workstreams in a fast-paced environment. 

  • Adaptability: Comfort with ambiguity and the ability to establish structure and process where none exists. 

  • Regulatory Awareness: Genuine interest in AI regulation and responsible AI, and in keeping ICW's posture current as expectations evolve. 

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS   

Office environment – no specific or unusual physical or environmental demands and employees are regularly required to sit, walk, stand, talk and hear.  

WORK ENVIRONMENT   

This position is based at ICW Group's Innovation Point campus in San Diego, CA. Occasional collaboration with remote team members and external partners via Microsoft Teams may be required. This position observes standard business hours with flexibility to support cross-time-zone engagements as needed.

 ABOUT ICW GROUP 
 ICW Group is a national, multi-line insurance carrier with an AM Best rating of 'A', approximately 1,300 employees, and headquarters in San Diego, California. ICW Group is executing an enterprise AI strategy that treats AI as core infrastructure: built on a single enterprise platform, governed by a single framework, and deployed under regulatory oversight from day one. As AI moves into underwriting, claims, and operational decisions, disciplined governance is what allows ICW to adopt AI quickly and defensibly. 
 ABOUT THE AI GOVERNANCE OFFICE 
 The AI Governance Management Office is ICW's standing execution and coordination function for artificial intelligence, sponsored by the SVP and Chief Digital and AI Officer. It serves the AI Governance Executive Committee (AIGEC) as its operational arm, turning AIGEC's policy, risk, and approval decisions into coordinated, well-governed delivery. The Office is the single operational home for AI intake, prioritization, coordination, enablement, and transparency. 
 The Office is also ICW's single coordination point for NAIC AI Systems Evaluation Tool response preparation. California, ICW's domiciliary state, is participating in the 2026 NAIC pilot, which creates an active compliance window for the organization's higher-risk AI systems in underwriting and claims. 
 PURPOSE OF THE JOB 
 The AI Governance Manager is an advanced professional individual contributor within the AI Governance Management Office, reporting to the Director of Cloud, AI, ML, and Enablement Platforms. This dedicated position works independently with limited oversight to administer, facilitate, and execute AI governance day to day: coordinating the governance committees, operating the intake-to-decision workflow, owning the AI Hub, and maintaining the governance artifacts and evidence that keep ICW audit-ready and regulator-ready. 
 Working closely with leadership and management at all levels, control functions, business owners, and external stakeholders, the AI Governance Manager makes governance practical and efficient so that teams move through it rather than around it. AIGEC and its subcommittees set policy, risk tolerance, and approvals; this role translates those decisions into consistent, well-documented execution, leads governance projects and processes, and provides guidance, coaching, and review of work products contributed by lower-level professionals and cross-functional partners.

 Governance Operations and Lifecycle Management 
 Coordinate and administer AIGEC and its AI Risk & Compliance and Third-Party AI Governance subcommittees: run the cadence (intake triage, risk review, forums), prepare review packs, and document decisions and action items to closure.

 Policy, Standards, Controls, and Inventory

 Administer the AI Systems Registry as the single audit-ready inventory of AI use cases, models, agents, and vendor AI, enforce the registry gate before build or deploy, guide business and technical owners through registry requirements, and coordinate model and system cards with lineage and classification for higher-risk systems. 
 AI Hub Ownership

 Training, Awareness, and Change Management 
 Coordinate role-based AI governance training, attestation, and change-triggered learning, support the governance champion network and cultural-change activities, and provide guidance, coaching, and review of governance work products to reinforce clear ownership and consistent governance behavior.

 This role does not have direct supervisory responsibilities.

 Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Information Technology, Risk Management, or related field, or equivalent experience. 
 Minimum of ten years of experience in program or project management, governance, risk, or compliance operations within a technology, IT, or regulated environment. 
 Demonstrated experience independently operating a governance, risk, or compliance program, including committee coordination, decision logging, evidence management, escalation management, and cross-functional process improvement. 
 Experience with AI/ML programs, digital transformation, or technology transformation initiatives, or a strong record of ramping quickly on new governance domains. 
 Advanced facilitation, stakeholder-management, and influencing skills, with the ability to navigate technical and business audiences at all levels of the organization, and influence practices, procedures, and policies at an operational level 
 Proficiency with collaboration and tracking tools such as Jira, Confluence, Smartsheet, or equivalent, and experience with SharePoint content management. 
 Excellent written and verbal communication, including the ability to produce executive-level packs, dashboards, regulatory response materials, and reporting. 
 Extensive working understanding of governance frameworks and compliance requirements in regulated industries, including the impact of governance decisions on business, technology, risk, and control functions 
 Experience in the insurance or financial services industry preferred. 
 Familiarity with AI governance frameworks: NIST AI RMF, ISO/IEC 42001, the NAIC AI Model Bulletin, and the NAIC AI Systems Evaluation Tool (Exhibits A through D) preferred. 
 Experience with NAIC regulatory requirements or Department of Insurance examination processes preferred. 
 Familiarity with the AI and ML platforms in use at ICW (AWS Bedrock, Snowflake Cortex) and enterprise AI tools (Claude Enterprise, Microsoft 365 Copilot) preferred. 
 Experience with SharePoint site design and enterprise portal management. 
 CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS 
 Risk, audit, or governance certification such as CRISC or CGEIT, or a project and program management certification such as PMP or PgMP, or SAFe / Lean Portfolio Management preferred. 
 KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS 
 Governance Discipline: Advanced ability to operate and improve governance processes, cadence, controls, and evidence, so decisions are defensible, repeatable, and scalable across the enterprise. 
 Facilitation: Ability to run committees, reviews, and cross-functional decisions across diverse technical and business teams, and to influence operational practices, procedures, and policies within and outside the immediate job function.

 Office environment – no specific or unusual physical or environmental demands and employees are regularly required to sit, walk, stand, talk and hear.

jobs.description_html:
Are you looking to make an impactful difference in your work, yourself, and your community? Why settle for just a job when you can land a career? At ICW Group, we are hiring team members who are ready to use their skills, curiosity, and drive to be part of our journey as we strive to transform the insurance carrier space. We're proud to be in business for over 50 years, and its change agents like yourself that will help us continue to deliver our mission to create the best insurance experience possible.


Headquartered in San Diego with regional offices located throughout the United States, ICW Group has been named for the twelfth consecutive year in a row and for the 20th time overall as a Top 50 performing P&C organization offering the stability of a large, profitable and growing company combined with a focus on all things people. It's our team members who make us an employer of choice and the vibrant company we are today. We strive to make both our internal and external communities better everyday! Learn more about why you want to be here!


PURPOSE OF THE JOB

The Data Engineer II – Data Operations & Infrastructure owns the operational health of ICW Group's data platform stack. This role receives production workloads from development teams and is responsible for their ongoing run and maintain lifecycle—monitoring, incident response, platform administration, governance, and small operational enhancements. The role ensures uptime, reliability, data quality, and cost efficiency across the data ecosystem. 

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Production Support & Operational Reliability

    • Takes ownership of data pipelines and platform workloads after handoff from development teams, becoming the primary point of accountability for their production health.  ​
    • Provides day-to-day production support for on-premises and cloud-based data pipelines, ensuring continuity of operations, timely incident resolution, and adherence to defined SLAs. 

    • Monitors, triages, and resolves data pipeline failures, performance degradations, and platform alerts across the data tech stack. 

    • Performs root cause analysis on pipeline failures and data issues, implementing fixes to prevent recurrence. 

    • Validates runbooks and handoff documentation from development teams; identifies gaps and works with developers to close them prior to full operational ownership. 

    • Maintains and enhances production support documentation including runbooks, troubleshooting guides, SOPs, and knowledge transfer materials. 

    Data Platform Administration & Governance 

    • Administers the data warehouse/lakehouse environment including user/role management, warehouse configuration, resource monitoring, cost optimization, and security policies. 

    • Manages and maintains the transformation layer infrastructure including environment management, job scheduling, model execution monitoring, and performance troubleshooting. 

    • Administers and monitors orchestration tools to ensure reliable scheduling, execution health, and pipeline SLAs are met. 

    • Supports data ingestion tool administration including monitoring sync health, managing schema changes, and troubleshooting ingestion failures. 

    • Supports business intelligence platform administration, with expanded ownership as the platform matures. 

    • Oversees data quality monitoring tools, ensuring rules are maintained, alerts are actionable, and data quality SLAs are met. 

    • Performs platform hygiene and decluttering—removing deprecated objects, unused connectors, stale pipelines, and orphaned resources across the data tech stack. 

    Data Infrastructure Monitoring & Observability 

    • Leverages cloud monitoring services to monitor data infrastructure components, configure alarms, maintain dashboards, and set up log-based alerting for pipeline health. 

    • Maintains and troubleshoots serverless functions that support data workflows from a data infrastructure perspective (overall environment/cloud infrastructure setup is owned by the Cloud Infrastructure team). 

    • Implements and manages application performance monitoring and observability tooling to provide end-to-end visibility into data platform performance, resource utilization, and anomaly detection. 

    • Builds and maintains operational dashboards and alerting frameworks to proactively identify and resolve data infrastructure issues before they impact downstream consumers. 

    Small Enhancements & Continuous Improvement 

    • Implements small operational enhancements to existing data pipelines—configuration updates, performance tuning, parameter changes, and minor fixes as defined by the team. 

    • Supports data ingestion workflows including monitoring connector health and adjusting configurations for operational needs. 

    • Supports regulatory reporting data initiatives from a data operations and pipeline reliability perspective. 

    • Identifies and implements operational improvements—automating manual processes, improving alerting coverage, and reducing mean time to resolution (MTTR). 

    Collaboration & Coordination 

    • Works closely with Data Engineering development teams to receive production handoffs, validate runbooks, and ensure smooth transitions from development to operations. 

    • Partners with Enterprise Architecture, Technology, Cloud Infrastructure, and Project teams to ensure operational consistency while maintaining data governance requirements. 

    • Contributes to data governance and data quality best practices including operational reviews, incident post-mortems, and continuous improvement initiatives. 

    SUPERVISORY RESPONISBILITIES 

    This role does not have supervisory responsibilities. 

    EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE 

    Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Applied Mathematics, Engineering, or any other technology-related field required, or equivalent combination of education and experience. Minimum 3 years of experience in Data Engineering, data platform support or production support of data systems required.  

    Experience administering a data lakehouse or data warehouse platform with hands-on RBAC, user management, and platform governance responsibilities required. Insurance experience a plus. Must have a solid foundation in data engineering fundamentals including understanding of ETL/ELT patterns, data pipeline architecture, data modeling concepts, and SQL proficiency sufficient to troubleshoot, validate, and maintain production data systems. 

    CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS 

    • Data architecture or data engineering related certifications strongly desired. 

    • AWS Cloud Practitioner or more advanced AWS certification preferred. 

    • Cloud practitioner or more advanced cloud certification preferred. 

    • Certifications in any major data warehouse/lakehouse platform preferred. 

    • Observability or monitoring tool certification a plus. 

    Knowledge & Skills

    • Strong experience administering a data lakehouse or data warehouse platform (e.g., Snowflake, Databricks, Amazon Redshift, Google BigQuery, Azure Synapse, or similar). Must have hands-on knowledge of role-based access control (RBAC), user/role management, resource/compute configuration, performance monitoring, cost governance, and security policies. Snowflake-specific experience is a plus  

    • Solid understanding of data lakehouse/warehouse architecture—storage layers, compute separation, medallion/multi-layer patterns, partitioning, clustering, and optimization strategies. 

    • Hands-on experience with dbt (dbt Cloud or dbt Core) including job monitoring, environment configuration, and execution troubleshooting. 

    • Experience with Apache Airflow (or similar orchestration tools) including DAG monitoring, failure triage, infrastructure configuration, and troubleshooting. 

    • Experience with Fivetran (or similar managed ingestion tools) for connector monitoring and administration. 

    • Familiarity with DOMO administration and production support (or willingness to learn quickly). 

    • Proficiency with AWS CloudWatch for monitoring, logging, alarming, and dashboarding of data infrastructure components. 

    • Hands-on experience with AWS Lambda in the context of data infrastructure (e.g., event-driven triggers, lightweight operational functions, alerting integrations). 

    • Experience with Data Observability tools  for infrastructure monitoring, log management, and alerting. 

    • Ability to build and maintain observability frameworks for data platforms—including SLA monitoring, pipeline health dashboards, and incident alerting. 

    • Understanding of incident management practices—root cause analysis, runbook development, post-mortems, and escalation processes. 

    • Working knowledge of database & data warehouse concepts, including MS-SQL, PostgreSQL, and cloud-native warehouses. 

    • Understanding of ETL/ELT patterns, data modeling concepts, and data pipeline architecture sufficient to troubleshoot and maintain existing pipelines. 

    • Working knowledge of SQL for troubleshooting, data validation, and small enhancement work. 

    • Familiarity with Python or similar scripting languages for operational automation and small pipeline modifications. 

    • Experience with AWS technologies like S3, EC2, Glue, Lambda, CloudWatch, and related services. 

    • Exposure to or willingness to learn data technologies: Spark, Kafka, Talend, etc. 

    • Strong operational mindset—proactive in identifying potential issues before they become incidents; focused on reliability and uptime. 

    • Strong documentation skills—ability to create and maintain runbooks, SOPs, and knowledge base articles for production support. 

    • A self-starter mentality that thrives in a rapidly changing, fast-paced environment and tolerates ambiguity while demonstrating problem-solving. 

    • Strong analytical and time management skills. Self-motivated and able to handle tasks with minimal supervision. 

    • Must be organized, detail-oriented, and able to multi-task. Ability to work well under pressure and deliver results with tight deadlines and under changing priorities. 

    • Ability to cross-collaborate with multiple teams and offer value-added solutions to meet objectives. 

    • Strong verbal and written communication skills. 

    PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS 

    This job operates in a professional office environment.  While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to talk or hear. The employee frequently will sit, stand, walk, and bend during working hours. Requires manual and finger dexterity and eye-hand coordination. Required to lift and carry relatively light materials. Requires normal or corrected vision and hearing corrected to a normal range. Ability to work additional hours, as required. 

    WORK ENVIRONMENT   

    This position operates in an office environment and requires the frequent use of a computer, telephone, copier and other standard office equipment. 

    We are currently not offering employment sponsorship for this opportunity. 

    #LI-TP1 

    #LI-HYBRID 


The current range for this position is

$95,378.98 - $160,850.17

This range is exclusive of fringe benefits and potential bonuses. If hired at ICW Group, your final base salary compensation will be determined by factors unique to each candidate, including experience, education and the location of the role and considers employees performing substantially similar work.


WHY JOIN ICW GROUP?

  • Challenging work and the ability to make a difference
  • You will have a voice and feel a sense of belonging
  • We offer a competitive benefits package, with generous medical, dental, and vision plans as well as 401K retirement plans and company match
  • Bonus potential for all positions
  • Paid Time Off
  • Paid holidays throughout the calendar year
  • Want to continue learning? We’ll support you 100% 


ICW Group is committed to creating a diverse environment and is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. ICW Group will not discriminate against an applicant or employee on the basis of race, color, religion, national origin, ancestry, sex/gender, age, physical or mental disability, military or veteran status, genetic information, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, marital status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state or local law.

Are you looking to make an impactful difference in your work, yourself, and your community? Why settle for just a job when you can land a career? At ICW Group, we are hiring team members who are ready to use their skills, curiosity, and drive to be part of our journey as we strive to transform the insurance carrier space. Headquartered in San Diego with regional offices located throughout the United States, ICW Group has been named for the twelfth consecutive year in a row and for the 20th time overall as a Top 50 performing P&C organization offering the stability of a large, profitable and growing company combined with a focus on all things people. It's our team members who make us an employer of choice and the vibrant company we are today. We strive to make both our internal and external communities better everyday! Learn more about why you want to be here!


PURPOSE OF THE JOB

The Claims Examiner position handles a variety of claims with a focus on providing the highest level of service for policyholders and ICW Group to bring claims to an equitable conclusion within Company standards and best practice guidelines. The Claims Examiner works with a sense of urgency, understands insurance coverage concepts, and navigates the legal system with the support of counsel to drive strategic outcomes.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Manages all aspects of a moderately complex claims inventory

  • Effectively communicates with policyholders, agents, attorneys, and witnesses to gather information and provide the highest possible level of customer service.

  • Promptly investigates claims to determine exposure, works with appropriate experts and makes strategic recommendations.

  • Utilizes appropriate resolution tactics (e.g., mediation, negotiation, denial, litigation or offer) to proactively drive outstanding results.

  • Operates within the requirements of related state and/or the governing entity rules and regulations as well as internal claims handling policies and procedures. 

  •  Partners with defense counsel throughout the litigation process in line with ICW litigation guidelines while monitoring legal fees and costs

 All Claims Examiners:

  • Consistently provides exceptional customer service

  • Effectively collaborates with cross-functional Team Members for project and process discussions

  • Makes recommendations for streamlining processes

  • Ensures accuracy of data in claims system for compliance with applicable regulatory reporting

  • Provides knowledge transfer across the organization

At ICW Group, we are hiring team members who are ready to use their skills, curiosity, and drive to be part of our journey as we strive to transform the insurance carrier space. We're proud to be in business for over 50 years, and its change agents like yourself that will help us continue to deliver our mission to create the best insurance experience possible.


Headquartered in San Diego with regional offices located throughout the United States, ICW Group has been named for the twelfth consecutive year in a row and for the 20th time overall as a Top 50 performing P&C organization offering the stability of a large, profitable and growing company combined with a focus on all things people. It's our team members who make us an employer of choice and the vibrant company we are today. We strive to make both our internal and external communities better everyday! Learn more about why you want to be here!


PURPOSE OF THE JOB

The purpose of this role is to develop, manage, and grow a profitable book of business within assigned line(s) of business, while serving as a senior-level underwriting and distribution partner to agents and internal stakeholders.

Senior Business Development Underwriters are responsible for underwriting more complex risks within assigned line(s) of business (e.g., Workers’ Compensation or Commercial Package and its component coverages) and are expected to operate with a higher level of autonomy, authority, and judgment. In addition, this role plays a key leadership role in driving broader Commercial Lines growth by identifying cross-sell opportunities, promoting all Company products, and supporting agency and distribution strategy.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Underwriting & Portfolio Management

  • Underwrite, select, and price moderately complex to complex risks within assigned line(s) of business in accordance with Company guidelines

  • Maintain accountability for the profitability, growth, and retention of assigned portfolio

  • Evaluate detailed risk characteristics including operations, financials, management, and loss history

  • Exercise advanced underwriting judgment and authority to structure, price, and manage complex accounts

  • Utilize underwriting authority to apply appropriate pricing, credits/debits, deductibles, and alternative rating structures

  • Quote and explain complex pricing structures (e.g., retros, deductibles, large account programs) where applicable

  • Monitor portfolio performance and take proactive corrective action to achieve underwriting targets

  • Remain current on regulatory, rating, and coverage changes (e.g., WCIRB/NCCI, ISO/AAIS)

Business Development, Production & Distribution

  • Drive new business production and achieve growth objectives through proactive agency engagement, prospecting, and cross-sell execution

  • Develop, manage, and optimize a high-performing producer force aligned with Company strategy

  • Hold producers accountable for production, quality, and profitability expectations

  • Drive profitable sales across all Commercial Lines products, including increasing penetration of existing products and supporting new product introductions

  • Actively identify and lead cross-sell opportunities, partnering across underwriting teams to deliver total account solutions

  • Prospect, prequalify, and appoint new producers with strong alignment to target business segments

  • Set and manage production goals and performance expectations with key agency partners

  • Maintain deep knowledge of assigned territory, including competitor positioning and market dynamics

  • Influence and provide input on distribution strategy, product positioning, and market opportunities

Producer & Relationship Management

  • Serve as a lead Company representative with key and strategic agency partners

  • Build and maintain strong, collaborative relationships through regular agency engagement, presentations, and strategic planning

  • Lead complex account and pricing discussions with agents and insureds

  • Provide underwriting and distribution guidance to agents, including structuring solutions for more complex risks

  • Deliver high levels of responsiveness, service, and professionalism in all interactions

  • Present agency performance insights, growth opportunities, and strategic recommendations to internal leadership and agency partners

Leadership & Mentorship

  • Mentor and support the development of Business Development Underwriters and junior staff

  • Provide guidance on underwriting approach, agency management, and deal structure

  • Participate in training, onboarding, and knowledge sharing across the team

  • Contribute to special projects, product initiatives, and process improvements as assigned

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

This role does not have direct reports but is expected to mentor, influence, and provide guidance to junior team members.

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

Bachelor’s degree in Business, Finance, Risk Management, or related field, or equivalent experience.
Minimum 5 years underwriting experience required; 7+ years preferred, with demonstrated experience handling more complex risks and agency relationships.

CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS

Current driver’s license required.

KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS

  • Demonstrated success in building and managing high-value agency relationships and driving profitable growth

  • Proven ability to underwrite complex risks and apply advanced underwriting judgment

  • Strong business development, negotiation, and relationship management skills

  • Ability to balance advanced underwriting discipline within assigned line(s) of business with production and cross-sell expectations across Commercial Lines

  • Ability to evaluate submissions, financials, and loss data to support complex decision-making

  • Advanced knowledge of Commercial Lines products, including Workers’ Compensation and/or Commercial Package and its component coverages

  • Ability to mentor, coach, and influence others

  • Strong analytical, communication, and presentation skills

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS 

  • Office environment – no specific or unusual physical or environmental demands and employees are regularly required to sit, walk, stand, talk, and hear.

  • Role requires 50%-75% travel to meet with clients, attend industry events, and develop new business opportunities.

  • Travel is usually limited to automobile but occasional air travel is required.

  • Requires regular visits to outside locations such as producer's offices.

WORK ENVIRONMENT 

  • This position operates in an office environment and requires the frequent use of a computer, telephone, copier, and other standard office equipment. Requires the ability to work 20-30% of time from home.

The position may include other duties as assigned.
