jobs.description_html:
Are you looking to make an impactful difference in your work, yourself, and your community? Why settle for just a job when you can land a career? At ICW Group, we are hiring team members who are ready to use their skills, curiosity, and drive to be part of our  journey as we strive to transform the insurance  carrier space. We're proud to be in business for over 50 years, and its change agents like yourself that will help us continue to deliver our mission to create the best insurance experience possible.

Headquartered in San Diego with regional offices located throughout the United States, ICW Group has been named for ten consecutive years as a Top 50 performing P&C organization offering the stability of a large, profitable and growing company combined with a focus on all things people. It's our team members who make us an employer of choice and the vibrant company we are today. We strive to make both our  internal and external communities better everyday! Learn more about why you want to be here!

PURPOSE OF THE JOB

The Quality Engineer II is an established, technical professional who serves as the Quality Engineering lead for their assigned delivery team. This role takes complete ownership of the test strategy, planning, and quality outcomes for the team, ensuring that quality is engineered into every stage of the software delivery lifecycle. Working independently with limited supervision, the QE II drives shift-left practices within the team, builds and maintains automated test solutions, and sets quality objectives that directly impact department results. The role requires practical depth in test engineering, the ability to solve difficult and moderately complex problems by drawing from prior experience, and the capacity to coordinate quality activities, delegate tasks, and coach junior team members.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Own the complete test strategy and test planning for the assigned Projects – defining scope, approach, risk assessment, entry/exit criteria, and test coverage targets for each release and sprint.

  • Act as the QE lead within the team and drive quality discussions during grooming, sprint planning, and design reviews; set quality objectives; and ensure the team delivers against them.

  • Develop, execute, and maintain comprehensive test plans, test cases, and test scripts for functional, regression, integration, API, and exploratory testing.

  • Build, maintain, and extend automated test suites using frameworks such as Playwright for UI, Postman/Newman for API, following clean code practice.

  • Execute API-level testing including payload validation, error handling, and contract verification for in-house and third-party service integrations.

  • Contribute automated tests to CI/CD pipelines (Jenkins, GitHub Actions), supporting continuous testing across regression, smoke, and feature validation stages.

  • Validate data integrity across integrated systems including ETL pipelines, data transformations, and end-to-end data reconciliation.

  • Identify, record, and thoroughly document defects; perform root cause analysis by reviewing logs, stack traces, and database states to diagnose systemic issues.

  • Participate in code reviews to provide quality-focused feedback on testability, error handling, and edge-case coverage.

  • Recommend enhancements to testing processes, tools, and standards to improve efficiency and effectiveness within the POD and broader team.

  • Own test data management, mock services, and QA environment configurations for reliable, repeatable test execution.

  • Leverage AI tools to assist in test case generation, coverage analysis, and failure triage.

  • Track and report quality metrics including defect density, escape rate, test coverage, and automation progress. Uses data to influence quality decisions.

  • Coordinate quality activities with distributed teams and offshore/nearshore vendor partners on test assignments, status calls, and triage.

  • Coach, guide, and review the work of junior team members; provide training on quality engineering practices and tools.

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

This role does not have direct reports but may mentor and/or train less experienced members.

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

Bachelor’s degree in computer science, Information Systems, or related field (or equivalent experience); 3+ years in quality engineering or software testing with 2+ years in test automation.

CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS

N/A

KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS

  • Practical, hands-on proficiency in at least one programming language (Java, Python, JavaScript/TypeScript) with the ability to read, understand, and debug production code.

  • Demonstrated experience designing test strategies and owning end-to-end test planning for a product, team, or release.

  • Hands-on experience building and maintaining automated tests using Playwright, Selenium, Cypress, REST Assured, or Postman/Newman.

  • Solid understanding of API testing concepts: request/response validation, status codes, error handling, and RESTful service patterns.

  • Working knowledge of SQL and database concepts – ability to write queries for data validation, verify data transformations, and support ETL testing.

  • Experience contributing automated tests to CI/CD pipelines (Jenkins, GitHub Actions) and understanding of continuous testing principles.

  • Familiarity with version control (Git), branching strategies, and pull request workflows.

  • Understanding of the test automation pyramid and strategic allocation of coverage across unit, API, UI, and data layers.

  • Exposure to performance testing concepts and tools (JMeter, k6, or equivalent).

  • Awareness of AI-assisted testing tools and willingness to adopt AI workflows for test generation and defect analysis.

  • Solid understanding of Agile/Scrum practices, shift-left testing, and the software development lifecycle.

  • Ability to work independently on moderately complex assignments with limited supervision; strong problem-solving skills drawing from prior experience and analysis.

  • Good communication skills; able to influence within the team and communicate with contacts within and occasionally outside the department.

  • Demonstrated ability to coordinate quality tasks, delegate work, and review the output of junior team members.

  • Preferred skills include strong Insurance domain background, specifically in Claims Management and/or Insurance Billing business workflows.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS

Office environment – no specific or unusual physical or environmental demands and employees are regularly required to sit, walk, stand, talk, and hear.  Employees are required to reach with hands and arms; stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl.  Employees must occasionally lift and/or move up to 30 pounds.  Employees are required to have visual acuity and be capable of operating and viewing computers and other electronic devices for extended periods of time.

WORK ENVIRONMENT 

This position operates in an office environment and requires the frequent use of a computer, telephone, copier, and other standard office equipment.

 Participate in code reviews to provide quality-focused feedback on testability, error handling, and edge-case coverage.
 Recommend enhancements to testing processes, tools, and standards to improve efficiency and effectiveness within the POD and broader team.
 Own test data management, mock services, and QA environment configurations for reliable, repeatable test execution.
 Leverage AI tools to assist in test case generation, coverage analysis, and failure triage.
 Track and report quality metrics including defect density, escape rate, test coverage, and automation progress. Uses data to influence quality decisions.
 Coordinate quality activities with distributed teams and offshore/nearshore vendor partners on test assignments, status calls, and triage.
 Coach, guide, and review the work of junior team members; provide training on quality engineering practices and tools.

 This role does not have direct reports but may mentor and/or train less experienced members.
 EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE
 Bachelor’s degree in computer science, Information Systems, or related field (or equivalent experience); 3+ years in quality engineering or software testing with 2+ years in test automation.

 N/A

 Practical, hands-on proficiency in at least one programming language (Java, Python, JavaScript/TypeScript) with the ability to read, understand, and debug production code.
 Demonstrated experience designing test strategies and owning end-to-end test planning for a product, team, or release.
 Hands-on experience building and maintaining automated tests using Playwright, Selenium, Cypress, REST Assured, or Postman/Newman.
 Solid understanding of API testing concepts: request/response validation, status codes, error handling, and RESTful service patterns.
 Working knowledge of SQL and database concepts – ability to write queries for data validation, verify data transformations, and support ETL testing.
 Experience contributing automated tests to CI/CD pipelines (Jenkins, GitHub Actions) and understanding of continuous testing principles.
 Familiarity with version control (Git), branching strategies, and pull request workflows.
 Understanding of the test automation pyramid and strategic allocation of coverage across unit, API, UI, and data layers.
 Exposure to performance testing concepts and tools (JMeter, k6, or equivalent).

jobs.title: Senior Business Development Underwriter, Commercial Lines - NorCal
jobs.description_html:
Are you looking to make an impactful difference in your work, yourself, and your community? Why settle for just a job when you can land a career? At ICW Group, we are hiring team members who are ready to use their skills, curiosity, and drive to be part of our  journey as we strive to transform the insurance  carrier space. We're proud to be in business for over 50 years, and its change agents like yourself that will help us continue to deliver our mission to create the best insurance experience possible.

Headquartered in San Diego with regional offices located throughout the United States, ICW Group has been named for ten consecutive years as a Top 50 performing P&C organization offering the stability of a large, profitable and growing company combined with a focus on all things people. It's our team members who make us an employer of choice and the vibrant company we are today. We strive to make both our  internal and external communities better everyday! Learn more about why you want to be here!

PURPOSE OF THE JOB

The purpose of this role is to develop, manage, and grow a profitable book of business within assigned line(s) of business, while serving as a senior-level underwriting and distribution partner to agents and internal stakeholders.

Senior Business Development Underwriters are responsible for underwriting more complex risks within assigned line(s) of business (e.g., Workers’ Compensation or Commercial Package and its component coverages) and are expected to operate with a higher level of autonomy, authority, and judgment. In addition, this role plays a key leadership role in driving broader Commercial Lines growth by identifying cross-sell opportunities, promoting all Company products, and supporting agency and distribution strategy.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Underwriting & Portfolio Management

  • Underwrite, select, and price moderately complex to complex risks within assigned line(s) of business in accordance with Company guidelines

  • Maintain accountability for the profitability, growth, and retention of assigned portfolio

  • Evaluate detailed risk characteristics including operations, financials, management, and loss history

  • Exercise advanced underwriting judgment and authority to structure, price, and manage complex accounts

  • Utilize underwriting authority to apply appropriate pricing, credits/debits, deductibles, and alternative rating structures

  • Quote and explain complex pricing structures (e.g., retros, deductibles, large account programs) where applicable

  • Monitor portfolio performance and take proactive corrective action to achieve underwriting targets

  • Remain current on regulatory, rating, and coverage changes (e.g., WCIRB/NCCI, ISO/AAIS)

Business Development, Production & Distribution

  • Drive new business production and achieve growth objectives through proactive agency engagement, prospecting, and cross-sell execution

  • Develop, manage, and optimize a high-performing producer force aligned with Company strategy

  • Hold producers accountable for production, quality, and profitability expectations

  • Drive profitable sales across all Commercial Lines products, including increasing penetration of existing products and supporting new product introductions

  • Actively identify and lead cross-sell opportunities, partnering across underwriting teams to deliver total account solutions

  • Prospect, prequalify, and appoint new producers with strong alignment to target business segments

  • Set and manage production goals and performance expectations with key agency partners

  • Maintain deep knowledge of assigned territory, including competitor positioning and market dynamics

  • Influence and provide input on distribution strategy, product positioning, and market opportunities

Producer & Relationship Management

  • Serve as a lead Company representative with key and strategic agency partners

  • Build and maintain strong, collaborative relationships through regular agency engagement, presentations, and strategic planning

  • Lead complex account and pricing discussions with agents and insureds

  • Provide underwriting and distribution guidance to agents, including structuring solutions for more complex risks

  • Deliver high levels of responsiveness, service, and professionalism in all interactions

  • Present agency performance insights, growth opportunities, and strategic recommendations to internal leadership and agency partners

Leadership & Mentorship

  • Mentor and support the development of Business Development Underwriters and junior staff

  • Provide guidance on underwriting approach, agency management, and deal structure

  • Participate in training, onboarding, and knowledge sharing across the team

  • Contribute to special projects, product initiatives, and process improvements as assigned

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

This role does not have direct reports but is expected to mentor, influence, and provide guidance to junior team members.

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

Bachelor’s degree in Business, Finance, Risk Management, or related field, or equivalent experience.
Minimum 5 years underwriting experience required; 7+ years preferred, with demonstrated experience handling more complex risks and agency relationships.

CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS

Current driver’s license required.

KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS

  • Demonstrated success in building and managing high-value agency relationships and driving profitable growth

  • Proven ability to underwrite complex risks and apply advanced underwriting judgment

  • Strong business development, negotiation, and relationship management skills

  • Ability to balance advanced underwriting discipline within assigned line(s) of business with production and cross-sell expectations across Commercial Lines

  • Ability to evaluate submissions, financials, and loss data to support complex decision-making

  • Advanced knowledge of Commercial Lines products, including Workers’ Compensation and/or Commercial Package and its component coverages

  • Ability to mentor, coach, and influence others

  • Strong analytical, communication, and presentation skills

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS 

  • Office environment – no specific or unusual physical or environmental demands and employees are regularly required to sit, walk, stand, talk, and hear.

  • Role requires 50%-75% travel to meet with clients, attend industry events, and develop new business opportunities.

  • Travel is usually limited to automobile but occasional air travel is required.

  • Requires regular visits to outside locations such as producer's offices.

WORK ENVIRONMENT 

  • This position operates in an office environment and requires the frequent use of a computer, telephone, copier, and other standard office equipment. Requires the ability to work 20-30% of time from home.

This description is a general statement of essential job functions and responsibilities. The position may include other duties as assigned.

#LI-JF1 #LI-Hybrid

The current range for this position is

$104,125.20 - $175,599.98

This range is exclusive of fringe benefits and potential bonuses.  If hired at ICW Group, your final base salary compensation will be determined by factors unique to each candidate, including experience, education and the location of the role and considers employees performing substantially similar work.

WHY JOIN ICW GROUP? 

  • Challenging work and the ability to make a difference 

  • You will have a voice and feel a sense of belonging 

  • We offer a competitive benefits package, with generous medical, dental, and vision plans as well as 401K retirement plans and company match 

  • Bonus potential for all positions 

  • Paid Time Off

  • Paid holidays throughout the calendar year 

  • Want to continue learning? We’ll support you 100% 


ICW Group is committed to creating a diverse environment and is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. ICW Group will not discriminate against an applicant or employee on the basis of race, color, religion, national origin, ancestry, sex/gender, age, physical or mental disability, military or veteran status, genetic information, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, marital status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state or local law.

Underwriting

jobs.title: US Renewable Energy Claims Associate
jobs.description_html:
This is your opportunity to join AXIS Capital – a trusted global provider of specialty lines insurance and reinsurance.  We stand apart for our outstanding client service, intelligent risk taking and superior risk adjusted returns for our shareholders. We also proudly maintain an entrepreneurial, disciplined and ethical corporate culture.  As a member of AXIS, you join a team that is among the best in the industry.

At AXIS, we believe that we are only as strong as our people. We strive to create an inclusive and welcoming culture where employees of all backgrounds and from all walks of life feel comfortable and empowered to be themselves. This means that we bring our whole selves to work. 

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to any protected characteristic, including age, color, disability, ethnicity, gender identity, marital status, national origin, pregnancy, race, religion, sex, sexual orientation, veteran status, or any basis prohibited by the laws that govern its operations.

AXIS is seeking a US Renewable Energy Claims Associate to join our Global Markets Claims team. This developmental role supports the handling of renewable energy claims under the supervision of experienced claims professionals. The successful candidate will gain practical experience in claim investigation, coverage review, reserving, stakeholder communication, and claim resolution across first-party and third-party losses.

The role will help deliver the AXIS Global Markets Claims value proposition by working with clients, brokers, external adjusters, engineers, counsel, underwriters, actuaries, and operations colleagues. The trainee will support clear communication, accurate claim administration, and a premier claims service while developing the technical judgment required for progressively broader responsibility.

The successful candidate will:

• Support the handling of US Renewable Energy claims allocated to the trainee under the supervision of senior claims professionals.
• Assist with triage of first notification of loss and the timely engagement of appropriate adjusters, engineers, counsel, and other service providers.
• Review policy wordings and claim information to identify potential coverage considerations and escalate issues for senior review.
• Assist with claim investigations, exposure assessments, reserve recommendations, and resolution planning within delegated authority and supervision requirements.
• Maintain accurate, timely, and complete claim files in accordance with AXIS policies, procedures, and service standards.
• Monitor claim activity, document next steps, follow up on outstanding information, and escalate material developments promptly.
• Work closely with clients, brokers, independent adjusters, engineers, external legal advisors, and other experts to help maintain a premier claims service.
• Engage with underwriters, actuaries, operations, and other internal stakeholders in relation to claims, reporting, and management information.
• Support the review and validation of indemnity and expense payments to help ensure accurate and timely processing.
• Develop a working knowledge of renewable energy technologies, relevant legal frameworks, policy coverage, and claims handling practices.
• Meet agreed expectations for claim quality, productivity, diary management, and claims handling cycle time.
• Continue professional development through formal training, coaching, licensing, and practical claims experience.
• Demonstrate the AXIS behaviors that support and align with AXIS values: People, Decisiveness, Excellence, and Stronger Together.
 
KEY SKILLS & ABILITIES:

• Bachelor's degree or equivalent work experience preferred.
• One to three years of experience with a US insurer, broker, claims organization, renewable energy business, engineering firm, or related industry is preferred but not essential.
• Claims adjuster license preferred; willingness and ability to obtain and maintain licenses required by applicable states.
• Interest in commercial property, renewable energy, engineering, construction, or complex claims.
• Strong analytical, numerical, and solution-focused skills, with the ability to work accurately to deadlines.
• Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to present information clearly and concisely for the intended audience.
• Strong interpersonal skills and the ability to build effective relationships with internal and external stakeholders.
• Effective organization, planning, time management, and attention to detail.
• Ability to manage competing priorities and work effectively in a hybrid and self-directed environment.
• Proficiency with Excel, Word, and PowerPoint preferred; familiarity with Outlook, OneNote, and other Microsoft Office products is desirable.
• Integrity, professionalism, curiosity, willingness to learn, and a collaborative team approach.


For this position, we currently expect to offer a base salary in the range of X to Y (NY), [X to Y (GA), X to Y (CA)]. Your salary offer will be based on an assessment of a variety of factors including your specific experience and work location. 

In addition, you will be offered competitive target incentive compensation, with awards based on overall corporate and individual performance. On top of this, you will be eligible for a comprehensive and competitive benefits package which includes medical plans for you and your family, health and wellness programs, retirement plans, tuition reimbursement, paid vacation, and much more.  

Where this role is based in the United States of America, this role is [Exempt/Non-Exempt] for FLSA purposes.

This posting is for an existing vacancy.

Job Description

P2026CORP015 - Claim Specialist Subrogation

AXIS is seeking a Subrogation Claims Specialist to join our North America Claims team and support the continued expansion of AXIS’ recovery operations.  The successful Candidate will manage an inventory of moderate to high‑complexity subrogation claims, ensuring timely identification of recovery opportunities, thorough investigation, accurate liability assessment, and effective pursuit of recovery from responsible parties and insurers.

Essential Duties & Responsibilities


• Performs a combination of duties in accordance with departmental guidelines.    
• Reviews claim files to identify, evaluate, analyze, and interpret subrogation potential.
• Is responsible for subrogation activities including the identification and research of subrogation claims.
• Identifies legal liability and pursues, negotiates, and settles claims where subrogation is identified.
• Coordinates appropriate steps to secure evidence and ensure pursuit, development, and recovery of claims.  
• Interacts with policyholders, claimants, and witnesses to recommend and document the necessary information to move forward with subrogation or close a file.
• Assists claim handlers during the life of the claim file to request the necessary information needed to pursue subrogation.
• Works closely with our TPA and MGA’s to ensure that all avenues of subrogation are identified and pursued.
• May provide guidance and assistance to less experienced claims staff and TPA’s.

Skills, Knowledge and Abilities

• Advanced technical and product specific expertise, claims resolution skill and knowledge of insurance and claims principles, practices and procedures.
• Strong written and verbal communication, negotiation and presentation skills. Ability to effectively interact with all levels of internal and external business partners.
• Advanced analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to manage and prioritize multiple projects.

• Ability to deal with ambiguous situations and issues.

• Creativity in resolving unique and challenging business problems.

• Knowledge of Microsoft Office Suite and other business-related software.

• Ability to adapt to change and value diverse opinions and ideas.

• Ability to manage and prioritize multiple projects.

• Ability to evaluate claims based on a cost benefit analysis.

• Ability to fully comprehend complex claim facts and issues; and to further articulate analyses of claims in presentations to business partners and management as well as in internal reports.

• Ability to implement strategies with a proactive long-term view of business goals and objectives.

• Ability to successfully work in hybrid and self-directed work environment

•  Axis Culture and Values – everyday demonstrate the Axis behaviors that support and align with AXIS values: People, Decisiveness, Excellence and Stronger Together


Education and Experience

• Bachelor’s degree or minimum 5-7 years of equivalent claims handling/underwriting experience in lieu of degree

• Valid licenses by state as required and add states to certifications as needed

•  Experience or exposure to handling commercial Property claims on behalf of a syndicate, insurance company, broker, loss adjuster or solicitor preferred

Role Factors

Preferred candidates will be able to commute to an AXIS office. We are a hybrid work environment, in office 3 days a week.

For this position, we currently expect to offer a base salary in the range of $80,000.00 to $100,000.00(GA). Your salary offer will be based on an assessment of a variety of factors including your specific experience and work location.

North America Casualty Treaty Reinsurance Underwriter


Job Family Grouping

AXIS Re - Underwriting

Job Family

AXIS Re - Underwriting | Underwriters

How does this role contribute to our collective success?

Reporting to the Head of North America General Casualty and Workers Compensation, AXIS Re, the successful candidate will underwrite and manage a portfolio of North American General Casualty and Workers Compensation Treaty Reinsurance business. The role will contribute to Business Unit profit goals, portfolio strategy, client and broker engagement, and disciplined cycle management across General Liability, Workers Compensation, Commercial Auto Liability, Umbrella/Excess Liability, and other casualty classes within the team's appetite.

What will you do in this role?

·   Originate, analyze, price, structure, negotiate, and underwrite North America general casualty and workers compensation treaty business in accordance with underwriting guidelines, portfolio appetite, allocated authority, and established best practices.

·   Manage assigned renewals and new-business opportunities across proportional and non-proportional treaty structures, including quota share, surplus share, working excess, and catastrophe or clash protections, as applicable.

·   Assess cedent strategy, management, underwriting controls, distribution, claims practices, reserving, rate adequacy, exposure trends, and historical performance to develop a clear underwriting view.

·   Partner with actuarial, claims, contract wording, finance, and legal colleagues to evaluate treaty economics, key assumptions, terms and conditions, and potential volatility.

·   Build and maintain strong relationships with reinsurance intermediaries and cedent clients to support profitable business origination, retention, and long-term strategic partnerships.

·   Contribute to casualty strategy and portfolio management, including appetite, guidelines, aggregate and limit management, concentration monitoring, and deployment of capacity.

·   Monitor market conditions and casualty loss drivers, including social inflation, litigation trends, legal and regulatory developments, medical inflation, loss-cost trends, and changes in underlying policy terms.

·   Prepare clear underwriting referrals, portfolio updates, and recommendations for senior leadership and governance forums.

·   Participate in cedent underwriting audits, claims reviews, stewardship meetings, and ongoing monitoring of account performance.

·   Maintain accurate and timely underwriting documentation, pricing records, exposure data, and internal system entries.

·   Travel to service clients, meet brokers, conduct audits, and attend industry conferences and market events.

You may also be required to take on additional duties, responsibilities, and activities appropriate to the nature of this role.

About You

You are a hands-on casualty treaty underwriting professional with strong technical judgment and a record of building and managing a complex book of reinsurance business. You understand the treaty underwriting lifecycle, from submission review and portfolio analysis through pricing, structuring, negotiation, authorization, documentation, and post-bind monitoring. You bring professional presence, commercial judgment, and the ability to communicate, influence, and build relationships that add value to the AXIS Re portfolio and support longer-term strategic initiatives.

We encourage you to bring your own experience and expertise to the table. While there are qualifications and experiences we need you to have, we are open to discussing how your individual knowledge may help you succeed in this role and contribute to our goals.

What you need to have

·   Demonstrated casualty underwriting, reinsurance underwriting, broking, actuarial, or related experience with a strong understanding of North American casualty business.

·   Knowledge of General Casualty and Workers Compensation, with familiarity across Commercial Auto Liability, Umbrella/Excess Liability, General Liability and related casualty classes.

·   Working knowledge of actuarial and pricing concepts, including experience partnering with actuarial teams to evaluate and price reinsurance treaties.

·   Ability to assess exposure and experience data, loss development, rate and exposure change, limits, retentions, attachment points, and treaty economics.

·   Strong grasp of underlying policy forms, reinsurance contract wording, exclusions, claims issues, and the roles of claims, actuarial, legal, accounting, and finance in the underwriting process.

·   Ability to communicate complex technical concepts clearly to audiences at all levels, including executive leadership.

·   Strong analytical, negotiation, marketing, and influencing skills, with sound judgment when faced with ambiguity or changing priorities.

·   Client-focused approach and flexibility in developing solutions that meet client needs while maintaining underwriting discipline.

·   Excellent organizational skills and the ability to manage multiple submissions, renewals, and peak-period workflows.

·   Highly collaborative and versatile, with the ability to work effectively both independently and as part of a cross-functional team.

·   Ability to initiate and independently lead defined projects and portfolio initiatives.

·   Bachelor's degree in a relevant discipline or equivalent industry experience.

What we prefer you to have

·   CPCU, ARe, ACAS, FCAS, ARM, or other relevant industry designation.

·   A minimum of five years of casualty insurance, reinsurance underwriting, actuarial, claims, or broking experience.

·   Experience underwriting or analyzing both proportional and non-proportional casualty treaty structures.

·   Established relationships with reinsurance brokers and North American casualty insurers.

·   Effective strategic relationship management and portfolio management skills.

·   Advanced Excel capability, including lookup functions, PivotTables, and analysis across multiple data sets.

·   Experience building dashboards or data models using Power BI.

·   Experience with AI Assistants a plus. 

·   Based in the New York City area or another approved AXIS office location.

Role Factors

·   Travel to visit clients and brokers, conduct underwriting audits, and attend industry conferences. 

·   Be in the office, or visiting brokers or clients, three days per week.

·   Attend broker and client events as required, including evenings and some weekend travel. 

What we offer

For this position, we currently expect to offer a base salary in the range of $185,000 - $250,000. Your salary offer will be based on an assessment of a variety of factors, including your specific experience and work location.

In addition, you will be offered competitive target incentive compensation, with awards based on overall corporate performance and your individual performance. You will also be eligible for a comprehensive and competitive benefits package that includes medical plans for you and your family, health and wellness programs, retirement plans, tuition reimbursement, paid vacation, and more.

This role is exempt for FLSA purposes.

This posting is for an existing vacancy.

Technical Assistant 

Job Description:
The Technical Assistant plays a crucial role in supporting the underwriting process by assisting Underwriters (UWs) and Account Managers (AMs) with general underwriting administration, processing, and clerical/office support activities.

The role involves supporting the underwriting process by gathering and organizing insurance application information, managing documentation, assisting with policy issuance, providing technical support, and ensuring compliance with company guidelines and regulatory requirements. The TAs also communicate with clients/brokers and collaborate with team members ensuring optimal customer service.

About the Team

You will join a collaborative team of Technical Assistants with diverse professional backgrounds. Team members work collectively to share workloads, provide training and guidance, and support one another in delivering consistent, high-quality service.

The role involves supporting the underwriting process by gathering and organizing insurance application information, managing documentation, assisting with policy issuance, providing technical support, and ensuring compliance with company guidelines and regulatory requirements. The TAs also communicate with clients/brokers and collaborate with team members ensuring optimal customer service.


Key Duties & Responsibilities:

  • Data Gathering and Documentation:
  • Gather and organize information pertinent to insurance applications, including applicant details, risk factors, policy specifications. Assist in obtaining additional underwriting documents (subjectivities), through timely and diligent follow-ups.
  • Maintain a diary system to ensure prompt receipt of account information.
    • Conduct thorough reviews of underwriting documents and policies to ensure accuracy and compliance with company guidelines and regulatory requirements.
  • Adhere rigorously to compliance standards while maintaining accurate account files and underwriting documentation.
  • Policy Issuance, Processing and Technical Support:
    • Provide support in processing policy endorsements, renewals, cancellations, and other policy-related transactions.
    • Process and book endorsements including premium bearing endorsements within established company Service Level Agreement (SLA) guidelines.
    • Accurately input account information into Policy Issuance (PIL) and endorsement logs.
    • Utilize underwriting software for data input and report generation.
    • Create post-binding E-File in Insurance Desktop (IDT) and update the PIL with account information.
  • Process various notices and filings such as Broker of Record (BOR) notices, Direct Notices of Cancellation and Motor Carrier Filings.
  • Handle declination letters, loss control survey inspections and final premium audits.   
  • Client Engagement and Communication:
    • Engage with internal/external customers to request information, clarify details, and provide updates.
    • Serve as a point of contact for Operations team and underwriters, providing optimal customer service.
    • undefined
  • Team Support and Collaboration:
    • Provide backup support for TA team when needed.
    • Collaborate effectively with various departments and colleagues to address inquiries, resolve issues, and streamline workflow processes.

Please note that additional duties, responsibilities, and activities appropriate to the nature of this role may be required.


About You:

We encourage you to bring your own experience and expertise to the table, so while there are some qualifications and experiences, we need you to have, we are open to discussing how your individual knowledge might lend itself to fulfilling this role and help us achieve our goals.


What we're looking for from you:

  • High school diploma or equivalent required.      
  • Undergraduate degree in business, finance, or related field preferred, but not required.
  • Preferably a minimum 0-2 years’ experience in the commercial insurance industry.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite or similar software.
  • Strong aptitude for learning new computer/software programs.
  • Solid critical thinking skills and problem solving skills.
  • Demonstrates a positive, can-do attitude.
  • Good verbal, written, and interpersonal skills.
  • Strong customer service skills and a professional demeanour.

Critical Competencies:

  • Able to follow directions effectively.
  • Self-motivated and capable of working independently.
  • Skilled at prioritizing tasks and highly organized.
  • Collaborates effectively with team members to achieve goals.
  • Adaptable to change and maintains a positive approach in dynamic environments.
  • Attentive to detail and accuracy.
  • Capable of multitasking in a high-volume work environment.     
  • Committed to ongoing professional growth and development.

Role factors:

  •  In this role, you will typically be required to be in the office 3 days per week

What we offer:

You will be eligible for a comprehensive and competitive benefits package which includes medical plans for you and your family, health and wellness programs, retirement plans, tuition reimbursement, paid annual leave, and much more.

For this position, we currently expect to offer a base salary in the range of $45,000 to $55,000. Your salary offer will be based on an assessment of a variety of factors including your specific experience and work location. In addition, you will be offered competitive target incentive compensation, with awards based on overall corporate and individual performance. Where this role is based in the United States of America, this role is [Non-Exempt] for FLSA purposes.

jobs.description_html:
This is your opportunity to join AXIS Capital – a trusted global provider of specialty lines insurance and reinsurance.  We stand apart for our outstanding client service, intelligent risk taking and superior risk adjusted returns for our shareholders. We also proudly maintain an entrepreneurial, disciplined and ethical corporate culture.  As a member of AXIS, you join a team that is among the best in the industry.

Senior Underwriter – Ocean Marine Cargo
New York or Chicago


The Senior Underwriter, Ocean Marine Cargo will act within established guidelines to analyze, evaluate, price, and manage new and renewal business in support of the growth of the U.S. Ocean Marine Cargo portfolio. The initial focus will include Small and Middle Market, Large Complex Transit, Stock Throughput, and Excess Stock Exposure risks


The role will also support AXIS’s broader Marine Logistics capabilities, which complement traditional Cargo coverage by addressing liability exposures throughout the movement, handling, and storage of goods. Relevant experience may include Cargo Legal Liability, Warehouse Legal Liability, Errors & Omissions, Shipper’s Interest, and packaged logistics solutions.


Candidate Profile

The Senior Underwriter, Ocean Marine Cargo will be a hands-on technical underwriting professional with a demonstrated history of success within a leading commercial insurance carrier, building and managing a complex Ocean Marine Cargo portfolio.


Candidates should have strong relationships across Ocean Marine Cargo wholesale and retail broker channels and full lifecycle underwriting experience, including solicitation and evaluation of submissions, risk analysis, structuring terms and conditions, pricing, preparing and issuing indications, quotations and binders, and portfolio management.


Candidates with Marine Logistics or related supply-chain liability underwriting experience are especially attractive, including exposure to freight forwarders, logistics providers, warehouse operators, and transportation intermediaries. Experience with Cargo Legal Liability, Warehouse Legal Liability, Errors & Omissions, Shipper’s Interest, or packaged Marine Logistics solutions is highly desirable.


The successful candidate should understand how traditional Cargo exposures interact with transportation, warehousing, contractual liability, and logistics-related risks across the broader supply chain, allowing them to evaluate opportunities from both a cargo/property and logistics liability perspective

Key Duties and Responsibilities

  • Underwrite and manage complex Ocean Marine Cargo business, including Small and Middle Market, Large Complex Transit, Stock Throughput, and Excess Stock Exposure risks.
  • Evaluate Marine Logistics opportunities that complement the Ocean Cargo portfolio, including Cargo Legal Liability, Warehouse Legal Liability, Errors & Omissions, Shipper’s Interest, and packaged logistics solutions.
  • Assess supply-chain exposures involving freight forwarders, logistics providers, warehouse operators, transportation intermediaries, and other businesses involved in the movement, handling, and storage of goods.
  • Review contractual and operational exposures to determine appropriate coverage structure, limits, retentions, pricing, terms, conditions, and endorsements.
  • Work with brokers to identify cross-sell opportunities across Ocean Cargo and Logistics, and develop broader solutions for clients with complex supply-chain exposures.
  • Prospect for new business and develop strategies targeting Small to Middle Market and Large Complex Corporate risks.
  • Develop and maintain strong wholesale and retail broker relationships, using those relationships to generate submissions and expand the portfolio.

Required Experience

  • 5+ years of direct Ocean Marine Cargo underwriting experience.
  • Demonstrated experience building and managing complex Ocean Cargo business.

Job Description: Technology and AI Strategy Lead


How does this role contribute to our collective success?

AXIS is undertaking a multi-year transformation to strengthen how we operate,

serve customers, and create competitive advantage. Technology and AI are important enablers of this transformation, creating opportunities to improve operational effectiveness, support business growth, and enhance customer outcomes.


The Technology & AI Strategy Lead is responsible for shaping, maintaining, and driving execution of the enterprise technology and AI agenda in partnership with business, technology, data, risk, and functional leaders. The role owns the integrated strategic agenda, enterprise-level recommendations, strategic coherence, value framework, and executive decision support. It does not own delivery of individual products or programs; delivery remains with the relevant business and technology owners, and business leaders remain accountable for outcomes, adoption, and benefit realization.


The role provides independent analysis, subject matter expertise, and strategic recommendations that help leadership evaluate technology and AI opportunities, risks, and trade-offs. Success requires strong business acumen, strategic thinking, stakeholder engagement, and the ability to translate complex technology concepts into practical business implications and measurable outcomes.
________________________________________

Key Responsibilities


Technology & AI Strategy


  • Support the development and refinement of the technology and AI strategy aligned with enterprise and business objectives.
  • Partner with business and functional leaders to identify opportunities where technology and AI can improve business performance, operational effectiveness, and customer outcomes.
  • Analyze emerging technology and AI trends, market developments, and vendor capabilities to inform strategic recommendations.
  • Assess opportunities to improve engineering effectiveness, delivery consistency, automation, and modernization efforts.
  • Consider responsible AI, data governance, cybersecurity, privacy, operational resilience, and regulatory requirements when developing recommendations and strategic assessments.

Portfolio Prioritization & Strategic Coherence

  • Support the development and maintenance of technology and AI roadmaps aligned to business objectives and transformation priorities.
  • Evaluate proposed initiatives and business cases against strategic goals, resource capacity, risk considerations, and organizational readiness.
  • Identify dependencies, opportunities for alignment, and potential conflicts across initiatives and programs.
  • Develop analysis and recommendations to support planning, prioritization, and investment discussions.
  • Contribute strategic insights that help leaders evaluate business needs, risks, costs, and expected value.

Execution Discipline & Value Realization

  • Develop and challenge value frameworks to evaluate expected business value and measure outcomes from technology and AI initiatives.
  • Analyze initiative progress, adoption trends, risks, and dependencies and provide insights to stakeholders, included any needed course corrections.
  • Identify lessons learned and opportunities to scale successful practices and capabilities.
  • Refresh the enterprise roadmap and investment recommendations based on delivery evidence, realized outcomes, emerging risks, and organizational learning.
  • Prepare strategic analyses, presentations, and recommendations for executive team.

Stakeholder Engagement & Change Enablement

  • Develop strategies to drive adoption of technology and AI-enabled capabilities across the enterprise.
  • Build collaborative relationships across business, technology, data, finance, risk, and transformation teams.
  • Facilitate workshops, planning sessions, and stakeholder discussions related to technology and AI priorities.
  • Develop clear, business-focused communications and presentations that help leaders understand strategic opportunities and implications.
  • Support initiatives that improve organizational understanding and adoption of technology and AI capabilities.
  • Identify barriers to adoption and recommend actions that support successful organizational change.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Support cross-functional strategic initiatives through influence, coordination, and collaboration.
  • Serve as a trusted advisor on technology and AI strategy-related matters.
  • Contribute subject matter expertise and analysis to governance and planning discussions.
  • Help stakeholders evaluate opportunities, risks, implementation considerations, and long-term implications of strategic initiatives.
    _______________________________________

About You

  • Significant experience in technology strategy, digital transformation, AI enablement, business transformation, management consulting, or a related field.
  • Strong understanding of technology, data, and AI concepts and their application to business problems.
  • Demonstrated ability to analyze complex issues and develop practical, value-focused recommendations.
  • Experience evaluating business cases and connecting technology investments to business outcomes.
  • Strong analytical, strategic thinking, and problem-solving capabilities.
    Proven success influencing stakeholders and building alignment across matrixed organizations.
  • Excellent communication, facilitation, storytelling, and presentation skills, with experience engaging senior leaders.
  • Working knowledge of responsible AI, data governance, cybersecurity, privacy, operational resilience, and regulatory considerations.
  • Ability to balance strategic thinking with practical execution.
    Insurance, reinsurance, financial services, or other regulated-industry experience preferred.
  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience required; advanced degree preferred.
    ________________________________________

Role Factors

  • Requires close partnership with business, technology, transformation, risk, and functional teams.
  • Success depends on expertise, influence, relationship building, strategic judgment, and the ability to navigate complex business challenges.
  • Regular participation in planning sessions, strategy reviews, governance forums, and leadership communications.
  • Operates within established enterprise governance frameworks and provides recommendations and guidance to support decision making.
  • Works independently on complex assignments requiring assessment of multiple business, technology, operational, and risk considerations.
  • Planning horizon is primarily annual and aligned with strategic planning and investment cycles.

For this position, we currently expect to offer a base salary in the range of $250,000 to $275,000 (NY). Your salary offer will be based on an assessment of a variety of factors including your specific experience and work location. 


In addition, you will be offered competitive target incentive compensation, with awards based on overall corporate and individual performance. On top of this, you will be eligible for a comprehensive and competitive benefits package which includes medical plans for you and your family, health and wellness programs, retirement plans, tuition reimbursement, paid vacation, and much more.  


Where this role is based in the United States of America, this role is Exempt for FLSA purposes.

This posting is for an existing vacancy.

This is your opportunity to join AXIS Capital – a trusted global provider of specialty lines insurance and reinsurance.  We stand apart for our outstanding client service, intelligent risk taking and superior risk adjusted returns for our shareholders. Director, Talent Management & Workforce Readiness

Job Family Grouping: Human Resources

Job Family: Talent Development

Grade: F

How does this role contribute to our collective success?

This role designs and drives AXIS's talent management and workforce readiness agenda in partnership with HR and business leaders, ensuring the organization has the leadership, skills, capabilities, and talent required to deliver business priorities today and in the future. You will establish and continuously improve the frameworks, processes, and insights that support performance, talent, succession, and workforce decisions across the organization. This is a talent management role with a workforce readiness component; learning and development experience alone will not meet the requirements. Success will be measured through stronger leadership pipelines, improved workforce readiness, effective talent decisions, and the organization's ability to build the capabilities needed for future growth.


What will you do in this role?

·       You will design, drive, and continuously improve AXIS's core talent management processes, including goal setting, performance management, talent reviews, assessments, succession planning, and development planning. You will establish clear frameworks and governance that support high-quality talent decisions and stronger leadership pipelines.

·       You will drive workforce readiness efforts by helping the business understand the leadership, skills, capabilities, and talent needed to deliver future priorities. You will assess workforce gaps, use internal and external talent intelligence, and identify actions to build, buy, borrow, reskill, redeploy, or automate capabilities.

·       You will identify development needs and priorities through performance, talent, succession, assessment, and workforce planning insights. You will partner with the Head of Learning to ensure development programs and investments address the organization's most important leadership, skill, and capability gaps; this role does not own learning program design or delivery.

·       You will partner with business leaders, HR Business Partners, the COO organization, and transformation teams to assess the workforce impact of changes in business strategy, technology, AI, and how work gets done. You will translate those changes into clear recommendations for skills, roles, workforce planning, mobility, succession, and talent investments.

·       You will use talent data, workforce intelligence, assessments, and external market insights to identify risks and opportunities and provide practical recommendations to senior leaders. You will monitor the health and effectiveness of talent and workforce practices and use insights to improve them over time.

·       You will lead and develop the Talent Operations & HR Business Analyst, manage key external partners, and work across HR and the business to deliver priorities, strengthen manager capability, and drive adoption of talent management and workforce readiness practices.

You may also be required to take on additional duties, responsibilities and activities appropriate to the nature of this role.


About You:

We encourage you to bring your own experience and expertise to the table. While there are some qualifications and experiences we need you to have, we are open to discussing how your individual knowledge could help you fulfil this role and contribute to our goals.


What you need to have:

·       10+ years of progressive HR experience, including at least 5 years of direct responsibility for designing, leading, or significantly evolving core talent management processes such as performance management, talent reviews, assessments, succession planning, and development planning at an enterprise or business-unit level.

·       2+ years of experience translating business strategy into future workforce, skills, or capability requirements through strategic workforce planning, skills strategy, organization transformation, workforce analytics, or a closely related discipline.

·       Demonstrated experience designing and implementing talent frameworks, governance, and processes across multiple businesses, functions, or geographies.

·       Demonstrated experience influencing senior leaders and using talent data, workforce intelligence, and business insights to support decisions.

·       Experience assessing complex talent and workforce issues, identifying risks and opportunities, and translating findings into clear recommendations and actions.

·       Experience leading enterprise-wide change, managing competing priorities, and driving adoption through HR Business Partners and people managers.

·       Experience leading and developing a team member, managing external partners, and collaborating effectively across HR and the business.

·       Demonstrated ability to handle sensitive talent, assessment, succession, and workforce information with discretion and sound judgment.


What we prefer you to have:

·       Direct experience with strategic workforce planning, skills-based workforce strategies, talent intelligence, or workforce transformation. Candidates are not expected to have equal depth in talent management and workforce planning, but must demonstrate credible experience across both.

·       Experience assessing how AI, automation, and evolving ways of working affect roles, skills, capacity, and talent needs.

·       Experience using Workday or similar technology to support talent and workforce processes.

·       Experience selecting, implementing, or governing assessment solutions that support talent and leadership decisions.

·       Experience in insurance, financial services, or another highly regulated global industry.

Role Factors:

In this role, you will typically be required to:

Be in the office 3 days per week

Travel domestically and internationally as business needs require


What we offer:

For this position, we currently expect to offer a base salary in the range of $212,000 to 234,000 (NY/CT).

Your salary offer will be based on an assessment of a variety of factors including your specific experience and work location. In addition, you will be offered competitive target incentive compensation, with awards based on overall corporate and individual performance. On top of this, you will be eligible for a comprehensive and competitive benefits package which includes medical plans for you and your family, health and wellness programs, retirement plans, tuition reimbursement, paid vacation, and much more. Where this role is based in the United States of America, this role is Exempt for FLSA purposes.

This posting is for an existing vacancy.

  • Increased adoption of AI-enabled capabilities.

jobs.description_html:

We also proudly maintain an entrepreneurial, disciplined and ethical corporate culture.  As a member of AXIS, you join a team that is among the best in the industry.

At AXIS, we believe that we are only as strong as our people. We strive to create an inclusive and welcoming culture where employees of all backgrounds and from all walks of life feel comfortable and empowered to be themselves. This means that we bring our whole selves to work. 

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to any protected characteristic, including age, color, disability, ethnicity, gender identity, marital status, national origin, pregnancy, race, religion, sex, sexual orientation, veteran status, or any basis prohibited by the laws that govern its operations.

How does this role contribute to our collective success?
Data, analytics and AI are critical enablers of AXIS' strategic ambitions. The Insights & Analytics Lead – North America will be a hands-on technical leader who turns business questions into high-quality insights, analytical solutions and clear recommendations for North American underwriting teams.
This role is responsible for translating business requirements into well-defined data, analytics, data science and AI requirements. You will explore and analyse large and complex data sets, identify trends and opportunities, determine the most appropriate analytical approach, and communicate conclusions in ways that support better, faster and more informed decisions.
Working within an agile delivery model, you will partner closely with business stakeholders, Data Engineers, Data Scientists, AI Engineers, Architects and Technology experts to design, test and deliver solutions that are practical, scalable and aligned to measurable business outcomes.
Reporting to the Insights & Analytics Director – North America, you will combine technical depth, business understanding and strong delivery skills. You will provide day-to-day technical leadership on initiatives while remaining personally involved in analysis, solution design and the development of analytical outputs.

What will you do in this role?

  • Translate Business Needs into Analytical and AI Requirements
    Partner with North American underwriting and business teams to understand business objectives, decision points, pain points and opportunities.
  • Translate business requirements into clear data, analytics, data science and AI requirements, including hypotheses, data needs, analytical methods, success measures and delivery acceptance criteria.
  • Challenge and refine requests to ensure the proposed solution addresses the underlying business problem and is proportionate to the value and complexity involved.
  • Recommend the right approach for each problem, whether descriptive or diagnostic analysis, reporting and visualisation, predictive modelling, machine learning, generative AI or workflow automation.
  • Deliver Hands-On Analysis and Insight
  • Frame analytical questions, develop hypotheses, select appropriate methods and validate findings before drawing conclusions.
  • Convert analysis into practical recommendations, explaining the business implications, limitations and actions required.
  • Identify opportunities where advanced analytics, machine learning, generative AI or agentic capabilities could improve underwriting effectiveness, portfolio management, operational efficiency or customer outcomes.
  • Shape solution concepts and technical requirements, including use cases, user journeys, required data, model or AI behaviour, controls, evaluation criteria and expected business value.
  • Rapidly prototype analytical and AI-enabled solutions to test feasibility and value before wider development.
  • Work with Data Scientists and AI Engineers to support model development, testing, validation, deployment and ongoing performance monitoring.
  • Ensure solutions are explainable, fit-for-purpose and developed in line with AXIS data, AI governance, security and responsible AI requirements.
  • Work as an active member of cross-functional agile delivery teams, partnering closely with Data Engineers, AI Engineers, Data Scientists, Architects, Technology experts and business product owners.
  • Contribute technical analysis, solution design, backlog refinement, estimation, sprint planning, demonstrations, testing and retrospectives.
  • Promote reuse of common data products, analytical methods, models and components across the wider Insights & Analytics community.
  • Define and track outcome-focused success measures, using feedback and performance evidence to improve solutions after release.
  • Explain analytical and AI concepts in clear business language and build confidence in the appropriate use of data-driven insights.

Success Measures
Success in this role will be measured through:

  • Delivered solutions contribute to measurable improvements in underwriting effectiveness, portfolio insight, operational efficiency or customer outcomes.
  • Solutions use the right level of analytical sophistication for the problem and are practical, explainable and fit-for-purpose.
  • Strong collaboration and trusted working relationships are established across North America business teams, Data & Analytics and Technology.
  • Insights and solutions are adopted and used within day-to-day business decisions and workflows.
  • Analytical assets, methods and components are documented, reusable and continuously improved.

About you:
We encourage you to bring your own experience and expertise to the table. While there are qualifications and experiences we need you to have, we are open to discussing how your individual knowledge might help you fulfil this role and contribute to our goals.
What you need to have:

Experience

  • A minimum of 7 years’ experience in analytics, business intelligence, data science or AI roles, with substantial hands-on experience analysing complex data and delivering data-driven solutions.
  • A minimum of 3 years’ experience in the insurance or reinsurance industry, ideally partnering with underwriting, portfolio management or specialty insurance business functions.
  • Demonstrated experience translating ambiguous business problems into structured analytical, data science or AI requirements and deliverables.
  • Experience delivering analysis or analytical products from initial discovery and data exploration through to recommendation, implementation and adoption.
  • Experience working as part of a cross-functional agile delivery team with data engineering, AI engineering, data science, architecture and technology colleagues.
  • Experience communicating complex analysis and technical concepts to non-technical stakeholders through clear visualisations, written conclusions and presentations.
  • Strong practical skills in SQL and at least one analytical programming language, such as Python or R.
  • Good understanding of data science and machine learning methods, model evaluation and the lifecycle required to move analytical solutions into production.
  • A strong problem solver who combines technical depth with commercial judgement and a focus on practical business outcomes.
  • Clear and credible communicator who can present complex findings simply and adapt the message for technical and business audiences.
  • Collaborative and delivery-focused, with the ability to work effectively across business, Data & Analytics and Technology teams.
  • Comfortable working iteratively, managing ambiguity and balancing pace with quality, control and maintainability.

What we prefer you to have:

  • Experience in North American specialty or commercial insurance underwriting analytics.
  • Experience developing or deploying AI, machine learning or advanced analytical solutions into production in an underwriting or portfolio management context.
  • Experience with cloud data and AI platforms and modern development practices, such as version control, testing and reusable code.
  • Education: A degree or advanced degree in a relevant field, such as Data Science, Statistics, Mathematics, Economics, Business Analytics, Computer Science or a related discipline, or equivalent professional experience.

Role Factors:
Be in the office 3 days per week

For this position, we currently expect to offer a base salary in the range of $160,000 to $185,000. Your salary offer will be based on an assessment of a variety of factors including your specific experience and work location. 

In addition, you will be offered competitive target incentive compensation, with awards based on overall corporate and individual performance. On top of this, you will be eligible for a comprehensive and competitive benefits package which includes medical plans for you and your family, health and wellness programs, retirement plans, tuition reimbursement, paid vacation, and much more.  

This posting is for an existing vacancy.

jobs.description_html:
This is your opportunity to join AXIS Capital – a trusted global provider of specialty lines insurance and reinsurance.  We stand apart for our outstanding client service, intelligent risk taking and superior risk adjusted returns for our shareholders. We also proudly maintain an entrepreneurial, disciplined and ethical corporate culture.  As a member of AXIS, you join a team that is among the best in the industry.

At AXIS, we believe that we are only as strong as our people. We strive to create an inclusive and welcoming culture where employees of all backgrounds and from all walks of life feel comfortable and empowered to be themselves. This means that we bring our whole selves to work. 

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to any protected characteristic, including age, color, disability, ethnicity, gender identity, marital status, national origin, pregnancy, race, religion, sex, sexual orientation, veteran status, or any basis prohibited by the laws that govern its operations.

Claims Lead – Grade I

Job Family Grouping: Claims Group

Job Family: Claims Specialist

How does this role contribute to our collective success?

The Claims Specialist plays an important role in protecting AXIS Re's balance sheet, reputation, and client relationships through the timely, accurate, and consistent handling of reinsurance claims. The role supports effective claim resolution, sound reserving practices, and high-quality service to internal and external stakeholders while ensuring compliance with contractual obligations and regulatory requirements.

By working closely with underwriting, actuarial, finance, brokers, cedents, and fellow claims professionals, the Claims Specialist contributes to loss analysis, reserve monitoring, and portfolio understanding. Through disciplined claim management and effective communication, the role helps deliver reliable claims outcomes and supports informed business decision-making. Through effective communication and knowledge sharing, the Claims Specialist helps bridge the gap between claims activity, business strategy, and operational decision-making. The role transforms complex claims information, loss data, and emerging risk developments into practical insights that support underwriting, actuarial, finance, and management stakeholders.

Ultimately, the Claims Specialist helps AXIS Re maintain strong claims governance, operational excellence, and trusted client service while supporting the broader objectives of the Reinsurance Claims team.

What will you do in this role?


  • Handle assigned reinsurance claims and claim portfolios in accordance with AXIS Re claims guidelines, delegated authorities, contractual obligations, and regulatory requirements.
  • Ensure claims are promptly and accurately documented, evaluated, reserved, and processed throughout the claim lifecycle.
  • Analyze claim submissions, loss notices, and supporting documentation to assess coverage, liability, financial exposure, and reporting requirements.
  • Identify and escalate coverage issues, large losses, accumulation concerns, and other material developments in a timely manner.
  • Maintain case reserves and monitor claim activity and loss development on assigned accounts.
  • Partner with underwriting, actuarial, finance, and legal teams to support effective claim management and informed business decision making.
  • Communicate directly with brokers, cedants, and other stakeholders regarding claim developments, information requests, coverage matters, and reporting requirements.
  • Participate in claims audits, including audit planning, file selection, audit attendance, preparation of audit reports, and communication of findings and recommendations.
  • Monitor legal, regulatory, and market developments that may impact claims handling, reserving practices, or portfolio performance.
  • Maintain high-quality claim files and ensure accurate, complete, and reliable claims data within company systems.
  • Contribute to management reporting, portfolio reviews, and other initiatives that support effective oversight of the claims portfolio.
  • Build and maintain strong working relationships with internal and external stakeholders, including underwriting, actuarial, finance, brokers, cedants, auditors, and service providers.
  • Support continuous improvement initiatives that enhance claims handling practices, operational efficiency, reporting capabilities, and data quality.
  • Assist in the development and maintenance of training materials, desk guides, reference tools, and process documentation to promote consistency and operational effectiveness across the Claims team.
  • Translate complex claims, coverage, legal, and reserving concepts into clear and concise communications tailored to a variety of business audiences.
  • Support the effective use of data, reporting tools, automation, and emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence solutions, to improve workflows and business processes.
  • Collaborate across global teams and functions to improve the quality, consistency, accessibility, and usability of claims information.
  • Contribute to a culture of learning, collaboration, and continuous professional development by sharing knowledge, best practices, and lessons learned.

You may also be required to take on additional duties, responsibilities and activities appropriate to the nature of this role.

About You:

We encourage you to bring your own experience and expertise to the table, so while there are some qualifications and experiences we need you to have, we are open to discussing how your individual knowledge might lend itself to fulfilling this role and help us achieve our goals.


What you need to have:

  • Minimum 3 years of experience in insurance and/or reinsurance claims handling.
  • Good understanding of insurance and reinsurance principles, coverage analysis, and claims handling practices.
  • Working knowledge of legal processes and laws applicable to insurance claims.
  • Familiarity with reinsurance customs and practices and laws applicable to reinsurance.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
  • Effective written and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities and work collaboratively in a team environment.
  • Strong attention to detail and organizational skills.
  • Experience using claims management systems; knowledge of SICS is beneficial.

What we prefer you to have:

  • Experience handling casualty, professional liability, cyber, specialty, or other complex insurance and reinsurance claims.
  • Experience participating in claims audits, portfolio reviews, or file quality assurance initiatives.
  • Experience working directly with brokers, cedants, reinsurers, underwriters, or other external stakeholders.
  • Strong proficiency with Microsoft Excel and familiarity with data visualization, reporting, or analytics tools such as Power BI.
  • Experience working in data-intensive environments and leveraging information to support business, operational, or claims-related decision making.
  • Familiarity with B2B operational processes and stakeholder engagement.
  • Interest in or experience supporting the use of automation, data solutions, artificial intelligence, or other emerging technologies within insurance or financial services environments.
  • Experience developing training materials, process documentation, job aids, or knowledge-sharing resources.
  • Demonstrated ability to communicate complex technical, legal, financial, or operational concepts to a variety of audiences.
  • Experience supporting onboarding, mentoring, coaching, or training initiatives within a professional environment.
  • Knowledge of emerging issues, market developments, and trends affecting the insurance and reinsurance industry.
  • Juris Doctor (JD) designation preferred but not required.

Role Factors:

In this role, you will typically be required to:

  • Maintain a regular onsite presence of a minimum of three days per week, in line with AXIS Re office attendance expectations.
  • Travel occasionally to support claims audits, market meetings, and stakeholder engagement activities.
  • Build and maintain effective working relationships with internal stakeholders including Underwriting, Actuarial, Finance, and Legal, as well as external partners such as cedants, brokers, auditors, and service providers.

What we offer:

For this position, we currently expect to offer a base salary in the range of $90,000 to $120,000. The specific salary offer will be based on an assessment of a variety of factors, including the experience of the successful candidate and work location. In addition, all employees are eligible for competitive incentive opportunities based on overall corporate and individual performance.

You will also be eligible for a comprehensive and competitive benefits package, including medical plans for employees and their families, health and wellness programs, retirement plans, tuition reimbursement, paid annual leave, and much more.

This posting is for an existing vacancy.
